Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 1:

(p-82)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat az-Zukhruf. His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear,﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾.

We have already discussed the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah, the letters that open certain surahs) at the beginning of Surat Hud.

As for His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾, we have already discussed it in Surat ash-Shu'ara' in the commentary on His statement, exalted is He: ﴿That you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 194-195]. And in Surat az-Zumar, in the commentary on His statement, exalted is He: ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness﴾ [az-Zumar: 28], and the verse that follows.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 8:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed on.﴾

The pronoun in His saying "them" (minhum) refers to the people who were extravagant (al-musrifin), who were addressed in His saying: ﴿Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you, turning away from you, because you are a people who exceed limits?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 5]. In this there is what the scholars of rhetoric (ulama' al-balaghah) call iltifat (the shift) from address (khitab) to the third person (ghaybah).

His saying "stronger than them" (ashadda minhum) is the direct object of "We destroyed" (ahlakna). Its origin is an adjective (na't) of an omitted noun, and the estimate is: "So We destroyed a people stronger than them in might," in accordance with the saying of Ibn Malik in al-Khulasah (the Alfiyyah):

"What is understood from the modified and the modifier may be omitted; in the modifier it is rare."

His saying "in might" (batshan) is a specification (tamyiz) transferred from the subject (fa'il), in accordance with his saying in al-Khulasah: "The agent's meaning is put in the accusative with the comparative form (af'al), like 'you are higher in rank' (anta a'la manzilan)."

Al-batsh (might) originally means seizing with violence and severity.

The meaning: So We destroyed a people who were stronger in might than the disbelievers of Makkah, who denied Our Prophet because of their denial of their messengers. So let the disbelievers who have denied you beware lest We destroy them for that reason, just as We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, that is, more in number, in equipment and in strength.

Thus the weaker and fewer should take warning from the destruction of the stronger and more numerous.

His saying in this noble verse: "and the example of the former peoples has passed on" means their characteristic, which is their complete annihilation because of their denial of the messengers.

The saying of one who said: "the example of the former peoples" means their punishment and their practice (sunnah), and this returns in meaning to that.

What this noble verse contains of threat to the disbelievers who denied Muhammad (ﷺ), that Allah destroyed those who were stronger than them, so that they would beware lest the like of what was done to those be done to them, has been clarified in other verses,

such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they stirred up the earth and cultivated it more than these have cultivated it﴾ [ar-Rum: 9].

And His saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and greater in strength and in traces upon the earth﴾ [Ghafir: 82].

And His saying: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth as We have not established you, and We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain...﴾ to His saying: ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins﴾ [al-An'am: 6].

And His saying: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them, yet they denied My messengers, so how was My rejection?﴾ [Saba': 45].

And His saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, and they were stronger than them in might? Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾ [Fatir: 44].

As for His saying in this noble verse: "and the example of the former peoples has passed on," what this noble verse contains of threat to the disbelievers of Makkah who denied Muhammad (ﷺ), in regard to His destroying them and His practice concerning them, which is punishment and the rooting-out torment, has been clarified in other verses,

such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had, and there befell them what they used to mock. And when they saw Our might, they said: "We believe in Allah alone and reject what we used to associate with Him." But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the practice of Allah which has passed among His servants, and there the disbelievers lost﴾ [Ghafir: 83–85].

And His saying: ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that the practice of the former peoples should come upon them﴾ [al-Kahf: 55].

And His saying: (p-84) ﴿So when they angered Us, We took vengeance upon them and drowned them all, and We made them a precedent and an example for the later ones﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 55–56].

We have already presented some verses indicating this in surah al-Ma'idah, in discussing His saying: ﴿For this reason We decreed for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 32].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Mighty, the All-Knowing."﴾

We have already presented, at length, the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright.﴾

**Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah al-Zukhruf (43), verse 10:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He who made the earth for you a cradle (mahdan), and made for you therein roads that you may be guided﴾.

The seven readers (al-Sab'ah, the seven canonical readers) differ on this word. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read *mahdan* with a fatḥah on the *mīm* and a sukūn on the *hāʾ*. The rest of the seven read *mihādan* with a kasrah on the *mīm*, a fatḥah on the *hāʾ*, and an alif after it. Both forms have the same meaning, which is "bedding" (al-firāsh).

In this noble verse, may He be exalted, mentions that He made the earth a *mahd* for the children of Ādam, meaning a bedding, and that He made for them therein *subul*, meaning roads, so that they may walk and travel in them, and thereby reach from one region to another. These two matters contained in this noble verse, namely that He, exalted is He, made the earth a bedding for the children of Ādam and made for them therein roads so that they may pass through from one region to another, are made clear in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made the earth for you a spread-out carpet, that you may traverse therein broad roads﴾ [Nūḥ: 19–20]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with them, and We made therein broad passageways as paths, that they may be guided﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 31].

He also mentioned that the earth is a bedding for the children of Ādam in many verses, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the earth – We spread it out, and how excellent are the Spreaders﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 48].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He who made the earth for you a bed and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah is He who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a canopy﴾, the verse [Ghāfir: 64].

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Naḥl", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: (p-85) ﴿And He cast into the earth firmly set mountains lest it shake with you, and rivers and roads that you may be guided﴾ [al-Naḥl: 15].

The Almighty's statement: ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in measure, and We revive a dead land with it. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾

What this noble verse contains, namely the indication that the revival of the earth after its death points to people being brought forth from their graves alive after death, in His words ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾, has been made clear in many verses. We have already presented it in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of the Almighty's words ﴿And He sends down water from the sky and brings forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22], along with the rest of the Qur'an's proofs of resurrection. We also clarified this in Surat al-Nahl, in the discussion of the Almighty's words ﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky; from it you have drink, and from it is vegetation in which you pasture your livestock﴾ [al-Nahl: 10]. We have done so in other places as well, and we have referred to this many times in this blessed book.

We have already presented in Surat al-Furqan the meaning of al-insha' (causing to rise) and al-nushur (the rising), and the various dialect usages concerning them, together with the Arabic evidence.

As for the Almighty's words in this noble verse, ﴿in measure﴾ (bi-qadar):

Some scholars said: that is, with a predetermined decree and divine ordainment.

Other scholars said: that is, in an amount by which the welfare of mankind is achieved. He did not make the water excessive, so that it would become a deluge destroying them, nor did He make it scant, below what is sufficient. Rather, He sent it down in a sufficient measure without harm, as the Almighty said: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth; and indeed, We are able to remove it﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18].

And the Almighty said: ﴿And there is nothing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, up to His words: ﴿and you are not its keepers﴾ [al-Hijr: 21–22].

Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 43, verse 12:

Allah's saying: ﴿Who created all the pairs (al-azwaj kulluha)﴾.

Al-azwaj are the kinds (al-asnaf), and the Arabs use the word zawj (pair, kind) for a kind.

Allah has explained that the pairs mentioned here include the kinds of plants, of the children of Adam, and of what no one knows but Allah. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:36].

He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿And He sent down water from the sky, and We brought forth with it pairs of various plants﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:53] (p-86).

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿When We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and produces of every lovely pair﴾ [al-Hajj 22:5]. That is, of every good kind among the kinds of plants.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down water from the sky and cause to grow therein of every noble pair﴾ [Luqman 31:10].

From the use of azwaj for kinds in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿And other [punishments] of similar kind, in pairs﴾ [Sad 38:58], and His saying: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to categories of them﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:131].

We have already presented part of this in Surat "al-Saffat," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions (azwajahum)﴾ [al-Saffat 37:22], and so on.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And He has made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾ ﴿So that you may sit firmly upon their backs, then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon them﴾.

We have already presented the many verses that clarify this in Surat "al-Mu'min" (Ghafir), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Allah is He who made cattle for you that you may ride some of them﴾ [Ghafir 40:79] and so on. The masculine singular pronoun in His saying ﴿upon its backs﴾ and His saying ﴿when you are seated upon it﴾ refers to the word (ma) in His saying: ﴿And He has made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 13:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And that you may say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have it [by our efforts]."﴾

He, may He be exalted and high, means that He made for the children of Adam what they ride of the ships (al-fulk), which are the boats, and of the cattle, so that they may settle (li-yastawu), that is, rise up and sit upright upon their backs. Then they should remember in their hearts the blessing of their Lord upon them through those means of riding, and then they should say, with their tongues while understanding the meaning of what they say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have it [by our efforts].﴾

As for His saying, "Subhan" (Glory be to Him, tasbih, the declaration of God's transcendence), we have already explained its meaning clearly at the beginning of the surah of Bani Isra'il. It indicates the perfect and complete declaration of God's transcendence, the Exalted, above everything that does not befit His perfection and majesty. The reference in His saying "this" (hadha) returns to the wording "mā" in His saying ﴿what you ride﴾, and the plural "backs" (zuhur) was used in view of the meaning of "mā," because its meaning is general and encompassing of everything its relative clause includes, while its wording is singular. So the plural in the verse is according to its meaning, and the singular is according to its wording.

(p-87) His saying ﴿who has subjected this to us﴾ means: who has tamed for us this, which is what we ride of the cattle and ships. For if God had not tamed the cattle for them, they would not have been able to control them, and it is not hidden that the camel is stronger than the man. Likewise, if He had not tamed the sea for them and made the running of ships in it subject to them, they would not have been able to do any of that.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and we could not have it [by our efforts]﴾ means: we were not able to (muqrinin), that is, capable of it. The Arabs say: "aqrana al-rajulu lil-amr" and "aqranahu" when someone is capable of it and fit to undertake it, from their saying "aqrantu al-dabbata lil-dabbah," meaning that if you tie the two together with a rope, you are able to withstand the one, and you are not weaker than it so that it drags you; for the weak one, when it is bound by a rope (qaran), that is, a cord, together with the strong one, is dragged and cannot withstand it, as Jarir said:

"And the son of a she-camel (ibn al-labun) when he is bound in a cord (qaran) cannot withstand the assault of the mighty, heavy-necked stallions."

This meaning is well known in the speech of the Arabs. From it is the saying of 'Amr ibn Ma'di Karib, which Qutrub recited for this meaning:

"The tribes have known that 'Aqil [is] for us, in the calamities, one who is capable of [meeting] them."

And the saying of Ibn Harmah:

"She carried me, and she was capable [of it]; yet rarely is the bearing of the hardships of the enemy of the abandoned [wilderness] endured."

And the saying of another:

"You have mounted my untamed she-camels with insolence and injustice, and you are not capable of [taming] the unruly ones."

What this noble verse contains, that what was mentioned of ships and cattle, had God not tamed them for them, they would not have been able to control them and would not have been able to bear them, has been stated clearly in other verses. The Exalted said concerning riding the ship: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them of its likeness that which they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-42]. The Exalted said: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh flesh﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 14]. The Exalted said: ﴿God is He who subjected the sea for you so that ships may run upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Jathiyah: 12]. The Exalted said: ﴿And He subjected for you the ships to run in the sea by His command, and He subjected for you the rivers﴾ (p-88) to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 32]. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, and the ships that sail in the sea with that which benefits people﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 164]. The Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen that God has subjected to you what is on the earth and the ships running in the sea by His command, and He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾, and verses like these are many.

The Exalted said concerning the subjection of cattle: ﴿And We have tamed them for them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72]. The Exalted said: ﴿So when their sides fall [after slaughter], eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you that you may be grateful﴾ ﴿It is not their flesh nor their blood that reaches God, but piety from you reaches Him. Thus He has subjected them to you that you may glorify God for having guided you. And give good tidings to the doers of good﴾ [al-Hajj: 36-37]. And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion (juz') from among His servants﴾.

Some scholars said: "juz'" means equal (ʿidl) and likeness (naẓīr), referring to the idols and other objects of worship besides Allah.

Some scholars said: "juz'" means offspring (walad).

Some scholars said: "juz'" refers to daughters (al-banāt).

Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir of this verse, mentioned that al-juz' means a share (naṣīb), and cited in support of this the verse of al-An'am, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "This is for our partners"﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-An'am: 136].

The one who restricts this (ibn Kathir's opinion), may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears is that Ibn Kathir's statement here, may Allah have mercy on him, is not correct regarding this verse, because what is assigned to Allah in the verse of al-An'am is a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, whereas what is assigned to Him in this verse of al-Zukhruf is "a portion from among His servants," not from what He has created of crops and livestock.

And between the two matters there is a clear difference, as you see.

Also, the statement of Qatadah and those who agree with him, that the intended meaning of juz' is equal and likeness, meaning a partner, is not correct either, because the use of juz' to mean a likeness is not well known in the speech of the Arabs.

As for the meaning of juz' in the verse being offspring, and the meaning of offspring being specifically females, this is the verified (taḥqīq) position regarding the verse.

The use of juz' for offspring may be explained by two matters. The first: what some scholars of Arabic (ʿarabiyyah) mentioned, that the Arabs use juz' to mean daughters, and they say: "ajza'at al-mar'ah" when a woman gives birth to daughters, and "imra'ah mujzi'ah," meaning a woman who bears daughters. They said that from it is the saying of the poet:

"If a free woman gives birth (ajza'at) one day, there is no wonder; a free woman may sometimes bear a male."

And the saying of another:

"I married her to a daughter of al-Aws who bears daughters (mujzi'ah), in whose homes is the swaying of the pliant spear-shaft (al-ʿawsaj) with its sound."

Al-Zamakhshari denied this usage, saying: it is a lie and a fabrication against the Arabs.

He said in al-Kashshaf in his discussion of this noble verse: "Among the strange tafsirs is the interpretation of juz' as females, and the claim that juz' in the language of the Arabs is a name for females. It is nothing but a lie against the Arabs, a newly invented and fabricated usage. And it did not satisfy them until they derived from it (ajza'at al-mar'ah) and then made verses:

'If a free woman gives birth (ajza'at) one day, there is no wonder; I married her to a daughter of al-Aws who bears daughters.'"

End of his words, verbatim.

Ibn Manzur said in al-Lisan: In the Revealed Mighty Book: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion from among His servants﴾. Abu Ishaq said: it means those who made the angels daughters of Allah, exalted and sanctified is He above what they invent. He said: I have recited a verse which indicates that the meaning of juz' is the meaning of females; he said, and I do not know whether the verse is ancient or fabricated:

"If a free woman gives birth (ajza'at) one day, there is no wonder..."

The verse.

The meaning in His saying: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion from among His servants﴾ is that they assigned Allah's share of offspring to be females. He said: I did not find it in ancient poetry, nor did reliable Arab transmitters narrate it, and "ajza'at al-mar'ah" means she gave birth to females. Abu Hanifah recited:

"I married her to a daughter of al-Aws who bears daughters..."

The verse.

The purpose of the words of the author of al-Lisan has ended.

The apparent meaning of his speech, which he transmitted from al-Zajjaj, is that the saying "ajza'at al-mar'ah" when she gives birth to females is well known; that is why he mentioned it and mentioned the verse Abu Hanifah recited for it, as one who accepts it.

The second matter, and it is the verified position, God willing, is that the intended meaning of juz' in the verse is offspring, and that it was called by the name juz' because the branch is, as it were, a part of its origin, and the offspring is, as it were, a piece (biḍʿah) of the parent, as is not hidden.

As for the intended meaning of the offspring, expressed by juz' in the verse, being specifically females, the context clearly indicates this, because assigning the aforementioned portion to Allah from among His servants is exactly what Allah denounced most severely, and He rebuked its perpetrator with severe rebuke in His saying after it: ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you? And when one of them is given good tidings of what he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief... and he is not clear in dispute﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 16–18].

Shu'bah from ʿAsim read this letter as juz'an with a ḍammah on the zāy, and the rest of the seven read it with sukūn on it. Hamzah, when pausing, drops the hamzah by transferring its vowel to the zāy, with the tanwin deleted for pause.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates, and chosen sons for you?﴾.

(Am) here carries the meaning of the interrogative of denunciation (istifham al-inkar). When the disbelievers said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah," Allah denounced them in the strongest terms and rebuked them in the strongest manner, since they attributed offspring to Him, and then assigned to Him the lesser and more contemptible of the two kinds of offspring, namely the female, as He says here: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾. The female is the lower portion of offspring. (And chosen for you) you, i.e., He preferred you and gave you precedence (with sons), who are the higher portion of offspring.

This denunciation of them and rebuke for it has been made clear in many verses, such as His saying here: (p-91) ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17], meaning the female, as He clarified it by His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with grief﴾ [An-Nahl: 58]. Meaning: how do you assign to Allah females while, if one of you were given the good news that his wife had given birth to a female, his face would darken, meaning from distress, and he would be "filled with grief" (kazim), i.e., full of sorrow and anguish. And His saying here: ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and in dispute is not clear?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 18]. In it there is a severe denunciation and a great reproach to them: that, despite their attributing offspring to Him, exalted is He, they assigned to Him the lesser of the two kinds of offspring, the one who, because of his natural deficiency, is raised among ornaments, from ornaments (huli) and finery and various kinds of adornment, from his childhood to his adulthood, so that by such adornment he may compensate for his natural deficiency; and in dispute he is not clear, because the female generally cannot undertake the defense of her argument nor defend herself.

We have already explained this meaning, with its Arabic evidences, in the fullest clarity in the surah of "Bani Isra'il," in discussing His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [Al-Isra': 9].

• And His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters—exalted is He—while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [An-Nahl: 57].

• And His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾ [An-Nahl: 62].

• And His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then preferred you with sons and taken for Himself from the angels females? Indeed, you utter a terrible saying﴾ [Al-Isra': 40].

• And His saying: ﴿For you is the male, and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [An-Najm: 21–22].

• And His saying: ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons? Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses? Unquestionably, it is of their own falsehood that they say, 'Allah has begotten,' and indeed they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is wrong with you? How do you judge? Will you not then remember? Or do you have a clear authority? Then bring your book, if you should be truthful"﴾ [As-Saffat: 149–157].

We have previously presented many of the verses clarifying this meaning in the surah of "An-Nahl," in discussing His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters—exalted is He—while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [An-Nahl: 57]. The reason for expressing the female by "that which is given as a likeness to the Most Merciful" in His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17] is evident: because the daughters claimed would necessarily be of the same kind as those to whom they are attributed, since the parent and the offspring are of one kind, and each resembles the other in its attributes.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read this letter ("ʿinda" in "ʿinda al-Rahman") with a sukun on the nun and a fath on the dal, as an adverbial of place (zarf), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud [to worship Him]﴾ [al-A'raf: 206]. Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿alladhina hum ʿibadu al-Rahman﴾ with a kasra on the ʿayn, a ba' with a following alif, and a damma on the dal, as the plural of ʿabd (servant), like His saying: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility...﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], to the end of the verse.

As for His saying, ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾, the majority of the seven read (ashahidu) with a single hamza and a fath on the shin, except Nafi', who read (a'ushhidu) with two hamzas: the first open and clearly pronounced, and the second with a damma and softened, between between (bayna bayna). They said: an alif of insertion (alif al-idkhal) is placed between the two hamzas according to one of the two transmissions.

In this noble verse, may He be exalted, He has mentioned four matters:

The first: that the disbelievers fabricated against the angels that they are females, claiming that they are the daughters of Allah.

The second: that He rebuked them severely for this and denounced it in His saying: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾, meaning: were they present at the creation of Allah for them, so that they saw them as females?

The third: that their false testimony to this will be recorded against them.

The fourth: that they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.

These four matters contained in this noble verse are explained in other places in the Qur'an.

As for the first of them, which is that they believed the angels to be females, He, exalted, mentioned it in several places of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then preferred you with sons and taken for Himself females from the angels? Indeed, you say a terrible saying﴾ [al-Isra': 40]. And such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the names of females﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Najm: 27]. And His saying: ﴿So ask them: Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons? Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Saffat: 149-150]. And other verses besides these.

As for the second matter, which is His questioning them in the manner of denunciation, rebuke and reproach: did they witness the creation of the angels and attend it, so that they knew that they were created as females? He mentioned it in His saying: ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ [al-Saffat: 150]. And He, exalted, made clear that He did not make the disbelievers witness the creation of anything, in His saying: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Kahf: 51].

As for the third matter, which is that their testimony to that disbelief will be recorded against them, He, exalted, mentioned it in several places of His Book:

• Such as His saying: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12].

• And His saying: ﴿This Book of Ours speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We were having copied down what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29].

• And His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80].

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot﴾ [Yunus: 21].

• And His saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird [of fate] to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open﴾ to the end of the verse, ﴿Read your record﴾ [al-Isra': 13-14].

• And His saying: ﴿We will record what he says and extend for him of punishment an extension﴾ [Maryam: 79].

As for the fourth matter, which is that they will be questioned about that fabrication and disbelief, He mentioned it in verses of His Book:

• Such as His saying: ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13].

• And His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92-93].

• And His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44].

• And His saying: ﴿And they assign to that which they do not know a portion of what We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate﴾ [al-Nahl: 56].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them. They have no knowledge of that; they only guess."﴾

In this noble verse there is a well-known difficulty (ishkal). Its nature is that the saying of the disbelievers which Allah mentions here, namely His saying ﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 20], is, judging by its apparent meaning, a true statement. For if Allah had willed that they not worship them, they would not have worshipped them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him﴾ [al-An'am: 107]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have brought them together upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant﴾ [al-An'am: 35]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, to the end of the verse (p-94) [as-Sajdah: 13]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would all have believed together. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus: 99].

The difficulty mentioned in the verse of az-Zukhruf is exactly the same as that found in the verse of al-An'am and the verse of an-Nahl.

As for the verse of al-An'am, it is His saying: ﴿Those who associated others with Allah will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything."﴾ to the end of the verse [al-An'am: 148].

As for the verse of an-Nahl, it is His saying: ﴿And those who associated others with Allah said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers."﴾ to the end of the verse [an-Nahl: 35].

So when you know that the apparent meaning of the verse of az-Zukhruf, the verse of al-An'am and the verse of an-Nahl is that what the disbelievers said is true, and that if Allah had willed they would not have worshipped anything besides Him nor associated anything with Him, as we mentioned in the clear verses above, then know that the difficulty is that Allah explicitly declared them liars in this claim whose apparent meaning is true. He said in the verse of az-Zukhruf: ﴿They have no knowledge of that; they only guess﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 20], i.e., they lie. And He said in the verse of al-An'am: ﴿Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our might. Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can bring out to us? You follow only assumption, and you are only guessing."﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. And He said in the verse of an-Nahl: ﴿Likewise did those before them do. So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ [an-Nahl: 35].

It is known that what those before them did was disbelief in Allah, and lying against Allah by making partners for Him, and that He prohibited what He had not prohibited.

The answer to this is that the intent of the disbelievers by their saying: ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾, and their saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148], is that since Allah was able to prevent them from shirk and to guide them to faith, and did not prevent them from shirk, this indicates that He is pleased with their shirk, in their assumption.

(p-95) They said: "For if He were not pleased with it, He would have turned us away from it." So Allah's refutation of them in the aforementioned verses is directed at their claim that He is pleased with it, and Allah, majestic and exalted, refutes this claim in the aforementioned verses, and in His saying: ﴿And He does not approve disbelief for His servants﴾ [az-Zumar: 7].

Thus the disbelievers assumed that the cosmic, predestined will (al-iradah al-kawniyyah al-qadariyyah) entails approval, and this is a false assumption, and it is this in which Allah refuted them in the aforementioned verses.

Allah, exalted is He, has indicated these aforementioned verses, where He said in the verse of az-Zukhruf: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so they are holding fast to it?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 21], i.e., have We given them a Book indicating that We are content with them in that disbelief? Then He turned away from this with a turning of rejection, clarifying that their basis for that false claim is the blind imitation of their fathers, and that is in His saying: ﴿Rather, they say: "We found our fathers upon a community (ummah)"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 22], i.e., a way and a creed, which is disbelief and the worship of idols, ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps, guided.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 22].

So His saying about them, "guided," is the object of refutation, because Allah is only pleased with being guided, not with going astray.

The supposed guidance is founded on the blind imitation of the fathers, and its refutation will be explained shortly, if Allah wills.

Allah, exalted is He, said in the verse of an-Nahl after mentioning their aforementioned claim: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was determined.﴾ [an-Nahl: 36].

In this noble verse He made clear that He was not pleased with their disbelief, that He sent a messenger to every nation, and commanded them through his tongue to worship Allah alone and to avoid Taghut, i.e., to keep away from worshipping everything other than Him.

And that Allah guided some of them to worship Him alone, and that among them were some upon whom error was decreed, i.e., disbelief and wretchedness were established for them.

Allah, exalted is He, said in the verse of al-An'am: ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

(p-96) So His sole dominion over granting success and guidance is the conclusive argument over His creation; meaning, whomever We guide and favour with success, that is a bounty from Us and mercy.

And whomever We do not do that for, that is justice from Us and wisdom, because that was not a debt owed by Us to him, nor an obligation he deserves from Us. Rather, if We give that, it is bounty, and if We do not give it, it is justice.

The summary of this is that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, decreed the destinies of creation before creating them, and knew that some would end in wretchedness and some in happiness, a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.

He established the proof against all by sending the messengers and supporting them with miracles that leave no confusion regarding the truth, and the proof of Allah on His earth was thereby established against them.

Then He granted success to whom He willed, and did not grant success to those for whom eternal wretchedness had preceded in His knowledge, and He created for each of them power and will by which he can achieve good and evil, and He directed their power and wills, by His power and will, toward what had preceded in His knowledge of deeds of good that entail happiness, and deeds of evil that entail wretchedness.

So they did all that they did and performed all that they performed, obedient and choosing, not compelled nor coerced. ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills﴾ [76]. ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

The claim that the servant is compelled, having no will, is evidently untenable according to the general body of sound minds.

Among the greatest self-evident matters indicating this is that every sane person knows that there is a clear difference, self-evident and undeniable by any sane person, between voluntary movement and involuntary movement, such as the trembling of one who shakes.

And if you were to strike someone who claims that creatures are compelled, and gouge out his eye for example, and kill his son, and excuse yourself to him by compulsion, saying to him: "I am compelled and have no will in this evil that I did to you; rather it is the act of Allah, and I have no part in it," he would certainly not accept this claim from you without doubt.

Rather he would exaggerate in his desire to avenge himself upon you, saying: "This is by your will and your choice."

(p-97) Among the greatest decisive proofs indicating the falsehood of the doctrine of the Qadariyyah, and that the servant does not act independently of Allah's power and will, is that no one can deny Allah's knowledge of everything before it occurs, and the verses and hadiths indicating this are denied only by an obstinate person.

The foreknowledge of Allah of what occurs from the servant before it occurs is a decisive proof of the falsehood of that claim.

The clarification of this is that if you said to the Qadari: "If Allah's knowledge, in His eternal pre-existence, has related to your committing theft or fornication in such and such a place at such and such a time, and you, by your independent will in your assumption, without Allah's will, wished not to commit that theft or fornication whose occurrence was foreknown by Allah, can you act independently in that and turn Allah's knowledge into ignorance, such that what was foreknown by Him does not occur at its appointed time?"

The answer, without doubt, is that this is impossible in any way, as Allah said: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills﴾ [76]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

There is absolutely no difficulty in the fact that Allah creates for the servant a power and a will by which he can do or abstain, then Allah, by His power and will, directs the servant's power and will toward what His knowledge had preceded, so the servant comes to it obedient and choosing, neither coerced nor compelled, and not independent of it without Allah's power and will, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills.﴾

The debate that some have mentioned between Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini and 'Abd al-Jabbar the Mu'tazili clarifies this.

It is that 'Abd al-Jabbar said: "Glorified is He who is exalted above indecency," meaning that theft and fornication are not by Allah's will, because in his assumption He is too exalted for these vices to be by His will.

Abu Ishaq said: "A word of truth by which falsehood is intended."

Then he said: "Glorified is He in whose dominion nothing occurs except what He wills."

'Abd al-Jabbar said: "Do you think He wills it and then punishes me for it?"

Abu Ishaq said: "Do you think you do it compelled by Him? You are the Lord and He is the servant?"

(p-98) 'Abd al-Jabbar said: "What do you say if He calls me to guidance, but decrees evil upon me, calls me, yet shuts the door before me? Do you think He has done well or badly?"

Abu Ishaq said: "I see that this which prevented you, if it was a true right and obligation owed to you by Him, then He has wronged you and done evil, and He is far exalted above that with great exaltation. And if it was His pure dominion, then if He gives you, it is bounty, and if He withholds, it is justice."

Then 'Abd al-Jabbar was confounded, and those present said: "By Allah, there is no answer to this."

The substance of Abu Ishaq's answer, by which he silenced 'Abd al-Jabbar, is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

Some have mentioned that 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd was approached by a Bedouin who complained to him that his mount had been stolen, and asked him to pray to Allah to return it to him.

'Amr said, in substance: "O Allah, it has been stolen, and You did not will its theft, for You are too pure and too exalted to direct this wickedness."

The Bedouin said: "I adjure you by Allah, O man, to stop from this evil prayer of yours. If it was stolen and He did not will its theft, then He may will its return and it is not returned. I have no trust in a Lord in whose dominion occurs what He does not will." So he silenced him with a stone (i.e., left him with no reply).

We have mentioned this question in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab," in the discussion of the verse of al-An'am mentioned in this discussion, and in Surah ash-Shams in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-387) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy

Surah az-Zukhruf

His saying: ﴿They said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾

Their saying this is true, because their disbelief is by Allah's cosmic will, and Allah has declared explicitly that they are liars, when He said: ﴿They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 20].

We have already presented the answer clearly in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Those who associated others with Allah will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him."﴾ [al-An'am: 148].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they are holding fast to it?﴾.

(Am) here includes the meaning of the interrogative of denial. He - exalted is He - means that what the disbelievers claim, namely that they are upon the truth in their worship of idols and in their making the angels daughters of Allah, has no evidence for them. Therefore He denied that He had given them a Book which permits that, and denied that they were holding fast to that by a Book from Allah. So He denied this against them here, a denial that indicates the negation of holding fast to the mentioned Book, together with rebuke and reproach.

What this noble verse includes, that their aforementioned disbelief was not based on guidance from Allah, nor on a Book that Allah had sent down for it, has been made clear in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat "Fatir": (p-99) ﴿Say: "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?"﴾ [Fatir: 40] to the end of the verse.

And His saying in "al-Ahqaf": ﴿Say: "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this, or a remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 4].

And His saying in "ar-Rum": ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate with Him?﴾ [ar-Rum: 35].

And His saying in "as-Saffat": ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾ ﴿So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾ [as-Saffat: 156-157].

And His saying in "an-Naml": ﴿Is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and who provides for you from the sky and the earth, a god with Allah? Say: "Bring your proof, if you are truthful."﴾ [an-Naml: 64].

And His saying in "al-Hajj" and "Luqman": ﴿And among the people is one who argues about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾ [al-Hajj: 8] and [Luqman: 20].

And His saying in "al-An'am": ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring out for us? You follow only assumption, and you are only guessing."﴾ [al-An'am: 148].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We did not send before you a warner into any city except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ ﴿[The warner] said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?"﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "Qad aflaha al-mu'minun" (The Believers), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 44], and so on.

In surah "al-An'am" (The Cattle), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We placed in every city its greatest criminals﴾ [al-An'am: 123], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 24].

(p-100) Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'bah from 'Asim recited: (Qul awa law ji'tukum) with a damma on the qaf and a sukun on the lam, in the imperative form ("Say: even if I brought you...").

Ibn 'Amir and Hafs from 'Asim recited (Qala awa law ji'tukum) with a fatha on the qaf and the lam, with an alif between them, in the verbal past form ("He said...").

According to the reading of the majority, the meaning is: Say to them, O Prophet of Allah: Will you follow your fathers in disbelief and misguidance, even if I bring you something better guidance, i.e., a religion more guided than that upon which your fathers were? The form of comparative here is for absolute description, because their fathers had no guidance at all.

According to the reading of Ibn 'Amir and Hafs, the meaning is: He said, i.e., the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

We have clarified this meaning with its Arabic evidences many times in this blessed book.

What this noble verse contains of ridiculing the opinion of the disbelievers and showing the extent of their misguidance in blindly imitating their fathers in this manner has come clarified in many verses, such as His saying in "al-Baqarah" (The Cow): ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers had no understanding of anything and were not guided?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170]. And His saying in "al-Ma'idah" (The Table): ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 104].

In the verse of "Luqman," He, may He be exalted, clarified that what they found their fathers upon of disbelief and misguidance is a path of the Shaytan, calling them by following it to the punishment of the Blaze, and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers upon." Even though Shaytan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ [Luqman: 21]. Like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray, so they hastened in their footsteps﴾ [al-Saffat: 69-70]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had certainly given Ibrahim his sound judgment before, and We were well-acquainted with him. When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?" They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them." He said, "Indeed you were, you and your fathers, in manifest error"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 51-54]. The verses of this kind are many.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 26:

Allah's saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of what you worship, ﴿except He who created me, for He will guide me."﴾﴾

(p-101) In this noble verse, Allah - exalted and majestic is He - mentions that Abraham - upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace - said to his father and his people that he is free (bara', i.e. bari') of all the objects of worship which they worship besides Allah. That is, he is free of the worship of every object of worship, except the One who created and brought him into existence; He alone is his object of worship.

Allah has clarified this meaning which He mentioned about Abraham in other places of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿He said, "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me, and it is He who guides me"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 75-78]. And such as His saying: ﴿So when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free of what you associate with Allah. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ [al-An'am: 78-79].

Allah - exalted and majestic is He - added in Surah "al-Mumtahanah" his disavowal also of the worshippers, his enmity toward them, and his hatred of them for the sake of Allah. This is in His saying: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone."﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4].

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿so He will guide me﴾ is similar to His saying: ﴿He who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 78].

And His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ [as-Saffat: 99].

And His saying: ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who are astray."﴾ [al-An'am: 77].

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, I am free of what you worship, except He who created me﴾, i.e., "who brought me into being," indicates that none deserves worship except the Creator alone - exalted and majestic is He.

This meaning which this noble verse indicates is also indicated by other verses of the Book of Allah, such as:

- His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21].
- His saying: ﴿And fear Him who created you and the former generations﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 184].
- His saying: ﴿Or have they made for Allah partners who created like His creation, so the creation seemed similar to them? Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer."﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 16].
- His saying: ﴿Is He who creates like one who does not create?﴾ [an-Nahl: 17].
- His saying: ﴿Do they associate with Allah those who create nothing, while they are themselves created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 191].
- His saying: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion, and who created all things and decreed for them a precise measure. And they have taken, other than Him, deities that create nothing while they are created﴾ [al-Furqan: 2-3].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 28 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He made it a lasting word among his descendants, that they might return﴾ ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is sorcery, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾

The pronoun object in (jaʿalahā, "He made it") refers, in verification, to the word of faith that includes the meaning of "there is no god but Allah," which is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who originated me﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 26-27]. This is because "there is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh) is a negation and an affirmation. Its meaning of negation is disavowal of all objects of worship other than Allah in all kinds of worship.

This meaning is clarified in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship﴾.

Its meaning of affirmation is the singling out of Allah alone for all kinds of worship in the manner that He prescribed through the tongues of His messengers.

This meaning is clarified in His saying: ﴿except He who originated me, for He will guide me﴾.

The hidden pronoun of the subject in His saying: ﴿And He made it﴾ is a matter of difference:

Some said: it refers to Ibrahim, and this is the apparent meaning of the context.

Others said: it refers to Allah, may He be exalted.

According to the first view, the meaning is that Ibrahim made that word ﴿a lasting word among his descendants﴾, that is, among his offspring and the offspring of his offspring.

Ibrahim made it lasting among them because he brought this about through two matters. The first: his enjoining it upon his children, and they came to inherit this charge from him, so the predecessors among them enjoin it upon the successors, as Allah indicated by His saying: ﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Ibrahim except one who makes a fool of himself? And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds." And Ibrahim instructed his sons in it, and so did Jacob: "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130-132]. (p-103)

The second matter: his asking his Lord, may He be exalted, for faith and righteousness for his offspring,

• like His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." He said, "And from my descendants?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. That is: "And make from my descendants leaders as well,"

• and His saying, about him: ﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and [also] from my descendants﴾ [Ibrahim: 40].

• and His saying, about him: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ [Ibrahim: 35].

• and His saying, about him and Isma'il: ﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation to You,﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129].

Allah answered his supplication regarding the sending of the mentioned messenger by sending Muhammad (ﷺ).

For this reason it has come in the hadith from him (ﷺ) that he said: "I am the answer to Ibrahim's supplication."

Allah also made the prophets after Ibrahim from his descendants, as He said in surat al-ʿAnkabut: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 27]. He also said about him and about Nuh in surat al-Hadid: ﴿And We had sent Nuh and Ibrahim and placed in their descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-Hadid: 26].

According to the second view, that the pronoun refers to Allah, may He be exalted, there is no difficulty.

In this verse of az-Zukhruf, Allah, may He be exalted, has made clear that He did not answer Ibrahim's supplication for all of his descendants, and did not make the word lasting among all of his offspring. This is because the disbelievers of Makkah, who denied our Prophet (ﷺ), are from his offspring by the consensus of the scholars, and they denied him (ﷺ) and said that he was a sorcerer. Many of them died upon that. This is in His saying: ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these people﴾, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah and their fathers, ﴿until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger﴾, who is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is sorcery, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾

What this verse of az-Zukhruf indicates, that some of the offspring of Ibrahim did not have the mentioned word made lasting among them by Allah, is also indicated by other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying in al-Baqarah: (p-104) ﴿He said, "And from my descendants?" He said, "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. That is, the wrongdoers from the descendants of Ibrahim.

And His saying in as-Saffat: ﴿And We blessed him and Ishaq. And among their descendants are the good-doer and the one who clearly wrongs himself﴾ [as-Saffat: 113].

So the good-doer among them is the one in whom the word is lasting, and the one among them who clearly wrongs himself is not like that.

And His saying in an-Nisa': ﴿We had already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom and given them a great kingdom. So among them is he who believed in it, and among them is he who averted from it. And sufficient is Hell as a blaze﴾.

Allah, may He be exalted, has made clear in al-Hadid that those among them who are not guided are many, and that is in His saying: ﴿And We had sent Nuh and Ibrahim and placed in their descendants prophethood and the Book. So among them is one guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Hadid: 26].

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿that they might return﴾ means: He made the word lasting among them, so that those among them who have deviated and gone astray might return to the truth through the guidance of the believing, guided ones among them. This is because, as long as the truth remains in their whole body, the return of those who have deviated from it to it is hoped for and expected, as His saying indicates: ﴿that they might return﴾.

The hope mentioned is in relation to the children of Adam, because they do not know who will be guided and who will go astray.

al-Qurtubi said, in explaining this noble verse, that there is in the speech an inversion and reordering. The meaning is: ﴿for He will guide me﴾, ﴿that they might return﴾, ﴿And He made it a lasting word among his descendants that they might return﴾, that is, He said to them: they should repent from worshipping other than Allah. End of his words.

The clarification of his speech is that the meaning is: Ibrahim said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship," so that they might return from disbelief to the truth.

The pronoun in His saying "that they might return" according to this view refers to his father and his people.

(p-105) According to what we mentioned first, the pronoun refers to those among his descendants who went astray, because the astray ones among them are included in the term "descendants" (ʿaqib).

So the return of their pronoun to the descendants is free of difficulty. This view is the apparent meaning of the context, and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Issue

The apparent meaning of these noble verses that we have mentioned indicates that the meanings of "descendants" (ʿaqib), "offspring" (dhurriyyah), and "sons" (banun) are one and the same, because He said in some of them about Ibrahim: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ [Ibrahim: 35].

He also said about him in some of them: ﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and [also] from my descendants﴾ [Ibrahim: 40]. And in some: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 37]. And in some He said: ﴿and from my descendants﴾, and in some: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 27]. And in some: ﴿and made it a lasting word among his descendants﴾.

So the apparent and immediate meaning of the verses is that what is intended by "sons," "descendants," and "descendants (ʿaqib)" is one thing, because all of them are about one thing. By this you know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that whoever endows a waqf or gives charity to his sons, his descendants, or his ʿaqib, the ruling for that is one.

Some Qur'anic verses have indicated that the children of daughters enter into the name "descendants" (dhurriyyah) and the name "sons" (banun).

And since the Qur'an has indicated that the son of a daughter enters into the name "descendants" and "sons," and it is assumed that ʿaqib has the same meaning as them, this indicates that the children of daughters also enter into ʿaqib. Among the verses that indicate that the son of a daughter enters into the name "descendants" is His saying: ﴿And among his descendants: Dawud and Sulayman﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and ʿIsa and Ilyas﴾ [al-Anʿam: 84-85]. This is a clear Qur'anic text that the son of a daughter enters into the name "descendants," because ʿIsa, peace be upon him and our Prophet, is the son of a daughter, since he has no father.

Among the verses that indicate that the son of a daughter enters into the name "sons" is His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers and your daughters﴾ [an-Nisa': 23]. And His saying: ﴿and the daughters of your brother and the daughters of your sister﴾ [an-Nisa': 23]. Because the word "daughters" in all three terms includes the daughters of daughters and the daughters of their daughters, and there is no dispute about this among (p-106) the Muslims. It is a clear Qur'anic text on the equality of the daughters of their sons and the daughters of their daughters.

Thus it is established that the entry of the children of daughters into a waqf upon "descendants," "sons," and "ʿaqib" is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and one should not deviate from it.

The statements of the jurists of the cities, from the four imams and others, regarding the mentioned terms are well known, and whoever wishes to be informed of them should consult the books of the branches of the schools of law. We have not expanded on that discussion here, because we only want to mention here what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates in preference of it, and nothing more.

As for the word "walad" (child/son), the Qur'an indicates that the children of daughters do not enter into it.

This is in His saying: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ up to the end of the verse [an-Nisa': 11]. For His saying "concerning your children" does not include the children of daughters, and there is no dispute about this among the Muslims. It is a clear Qur'anic text that the children of daughters do not enter into the name "walad."

Although the majority of scholars hold that ʿaqib and walad are the same.

And there is no doubt that following the Qur'an is what is required of every Muslim.

As for the word "nasl" (progeny), the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is that it includes the children of daughters, because His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ ﴿who perfected everything He created and began the creation of man from clay﴾ ﴿then made his progeny from an extract of fluid, despised﴾ [as-Sajdah: 6-8] is apparent that the word "nasl" in the verse includes the children of daughters, as is not hidden.

The terms about which the scholars speak in this topic are eleven terms. We have mentioned five of them, namely: dhurriyyah, banun, ʿaqib, walad, and nasl. We have mentioned that four of them the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that the children of daughters enter into them, and one is contrary to that, namely walad.

As for the remaining six: they are āl and ahl, whose meaning is one; al-qarabah (kinship), al-ʿashirah (clan), al-qawm (people), and al-mawali (clients), and the statements of the scholars about them are inconsistent.

I do not now recall a definition that clearly distinguishes what enters into each of them and what exits from it, except in approximate terms, except for two of them, which are al-qarabah and al-ʿashirah.

As for al-qarabah, it is established in the Sahih that he (ﷺ) gave from the fifth of Khaybar to Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, "but not Banu ʿAbd Shams and Banu Nawfal," clarifying that this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. As was previously explained in surat al-Anfal in the discussion of this verse of the fifth.

As for al-ʿashirah, it is established in the Sahih from him (ﷺ), from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, that when His saying was revealed: ﴿And warn your nearest kindred﴾ [ash-Shuʿara': 214], the Prophet (ﷺ) climbed al-Safa and began calling out: "O Banu Fihr! O Banu ʿAdi!" to the branches of Quraysh until they gathered, the hadith. In it, the nearest kindred (al-ʿashirah al-aqrabin) is defined as all of Banu Fihr ibn Malik, who is his tenth-generation ancestor (ﷺ).

In the narration of Abu Hurayrah in the Sahih, when the mentioned verse was revealed, he said: "O assembly of Quraysh" or a similar phrase, the hadith. Quraysh are the descendants of Fihr ibn Malik. It is also said: the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah. The first is more apparent due to the mentioned hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and most scholars hold it.

Note

[If it is said]: You have mentioned that the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that the children of daughters enter into the word "banun" (sons), while the poet says to the contrary:

Our sons are the sons of our sons, and our daughters' sons are the sons of distant men.

Many people of jurisprudence cite the mentioned verse as if they accept it, and they say: among what clarifies its truth is that they are attributed to other men, who may have been enemies of the people of their mothers, and the child often follows his father and his clan in enmity toward his maternal uncles and hatred of them, as is known.

[Therefore the answer is] that a single person has two aspects. The meaning of the word "son" (ibn) has one specific aspect: that he was created from the water of this man, in a manner by which his lineage is attached to him. This meaning is denied of a man's maternal grandfather, so he is not called "son" in this sense. It is established for the father from whose water he was created. It has another aspect: that he is, in general, issued from this person, whether directly or through his son or daughter, however far down the line. In this sense, sonship is established for a daughter's son. This is the meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) intended in his saying about al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Indeed, this son of mine is a master," and so on. It is also the meaning intended in the Qur'anic verses, such as the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters﴾ [An-Nisa: 23]. And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and your brothers' daughters and your sisters' daughters﴾ [An-Nisa: 23]. And like the saying of Allah, the Exalted: (p-108) ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 55], and so on.

The words "daughters" and "sons" in all the verses mentioned include all the offspring of sons and daughters, however far down the line. They include them from the aspect mentioned and by the consideration mentioned, which is the application of the word "son" to everyone who has issued from the person in general, even through his daughters.

As for the verse of poetry mentioned, the intended meaning is the first aspect and the first consideration. The sons of daughters are not sons of their maternal grandfathers from that aspect or by that consideration, because they were not created from his water. Rather, they were created from the water of other men, who may be distant or may even be enemies.

Thus, by this consideration, the denial of sonship from the son of a daughter is valid. By the first consideration, the affirmation of sonship for him is valid, and there is no contradiction in the separation of the aspects.

Once you know the meaning of the two aspects mentioned, and that by considering one of them sonship is established for the son of a daughter, while by considering the other it is negated, then know that the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, this son of mine is a master," and the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿and your brothers' daughters and your sisters' daughters﴾ [An-Nisa: 23], and similar verses, are to be understood according to one of the two aspects.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 40] is to be understood according to the other aspect. That aspect is the one the poet means by his saying:

"And our daughters' sons are the sons of distant men."

What further clarifies this is that the tribes of the Arabs were sometimes at war and in fighting with one another, so the fighting would be between a man's paternal uncles and his maternal uncles. He would be with his own clan always against his maternal uncles, as in the verse mentioned.

Sometimes a man from among them would be with his maternal uncles, and they would treat him in a manner less than their treatment of their own sons, as Ghassan ibn Wa'lah clarified in his poetry, where he says:

"If you are among Sa'd, and your mother is partly from them,
then do not let your maternal uncle from Sa'd deceive you."

(p-109) "For the son of a people's sister, his vessel is tilted,
if he does not vie with his maternal uncle with a steadfast father."

His saying "his vessel is tilted" (muṣghin inā'uhu) comes from iṣghā', which means inclining. When a vessel is tilted and not left level, it holds only a little. So it is a metaphor for the lessening of his share among them and its scarcity.

On the basis of the two aspects mentioned, the disagreement of the Companions concerning the inheritance of the grandfather (jadd) and the brothers is to be understood. Whoever among them held that the grandfather is a father and blocks the brothers from inheritance was taking into account one of the two aspects. Whoever among them held that he is not a father and does not block the brothers was considering the other aspect.

We have not lengthened the discussion here regarding all the words mentioned, which are eleven words, for fear of prolixity, and because we have not found texts of revelation that define any of them precisely.

It is known that the word "qawm" (people), among these, the Qur'an has shown is specific to males to the exclusion of females. Women may enter it by way of subordination when it is accompanied by something indicating that.

For Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Let not a people ridicule another people, who may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 11]. His joining of "women" to "people" indicates that they are not included in the word "people."

A parallel to this from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And I do not know, and I suppose I shall not know,
whether the family of Hisn are a people or women."

As for the entry of women into "people" by way of subordination when accompanied by something that indicates this, it is clarified by the saying of Allah, the Exalted, concerning the Queen of Sheba: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had turned her away; indeed, she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [An-Naml: 43].

As for "mawali" (clients, kin, or those bound by allegiance), the Qur'an and the language have shown that "mawla" is applied to everyone who has a cause by which he is allied to and allies others.

For this reason Allah is described as the Mawla of the believers, because they ally themselves to Him through obedience, and He allies Himself to them through reward.

He negated the guardianship of obedience from the disbelievers in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿That is because Allah is the Mawla of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no mawla﴾ [Muhammad: 11].

(p-110) He affirmed for Himself over them the guardianship of dominion and power in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Mawla, and what they used to fabricate is lost to them﴾ [Al-An'am: 62, cited as 10 in the source]. Likewise, He affirmed for the Fire a guardianship over them in His saying: ﴿Your abode is the Fire; it is your mawla﴾ [Al-Hadid: 15].

Allah, the Exalted, applied the name "mawali" to the 'asabah (agnatic kin, male relatives on the father's side) in His saying: ﴿And for each We have appointed heirs (mawali) of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾ [An-Nisa: 33].

He applied the name "mawla" to relatives and the like in His saying: ﴿The day when no mawla will avail any mawla at all﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 41].

In Arabic speech, "mawali" is often applied to the 'asabah and to the son of a paternal uncle. From this is the saying of al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas ibn Utbah ibn Abi Lahab:

"Gently, sons of our paternal uncle, gently, our mawali;
do not reveal to us what was hidden."

And the saying of Tarafa ibn al-Abd:

"I know with a knowledge that is not mere supposition
that when a man's mawla is humiliated, he is humiliated."

The conclusion is that whoever says, "This is a waqf (endowment), or a charity, for my people (qawmi), or my mawali," then: if there is a specific custom (urf) there, it must be followed in that matter. If there is no custom, we know of no text from the Book or the Sunnah that defines this precisely.

The statements of the people of knowledge on this are well known in their proper places.

And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 31:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?" Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in rank, that some of them may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾

(And they say) means the disbelievers of Makkah said. (Why) means why not (lawla) ﴿was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man from the two cities﴾, meaning from one of the two cities, namely Makkah and al-Ta'if. (Of importance) — by his importance they meant the abundance of his wealth, the greatness of his standing, and the loftiness of his position among his people. The "great man" of Makkah whom they intended is al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Makhzum ibn Yaqazah ibn Murrah ibn Ka'b, and his lineage converges with that of the Prophet ﷺ at Murrah ibn Ka'b.

It has been said that he was 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf.

The great man of al-Ta'if was 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud. It has been said he was Habib ibn Amr ibn Umayr, and it has been said he was Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil, and other things have been said.

The clarification of the verse is that the disbelievers first denied that Allah would send a messenger from among mankind, as we have explained many times. Then, when they heard the evidence that Allah has sent to mankind only messengers from among mankind, they retreated from their proposal of sending angelic messengers to another proposal, namely that this Qur'an be sent down upon one of the two men mentioned.

This proposal indicates the extreme of their ignorance and the feebleness of their minds, in that they make abundance of wealth and status in this world a cause for deserving prophethood and the descent of revelation.
