For this reason they claimed that Muhammad ﷺ was not fit to receive this Qur'an, due to the scarcity of his wealth, and that one of the two men mentioned was more worthy than he ﷺ to have the Qur'an sent down upon him.

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted has shown the extent of their ignorance and the feebleness of their minds, by His saying: ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ The apparent and immediate meaning is that by "the mercy of your Lord" is meant prophethood and the sending down of revelation.

The use of "mercy" for this is repeated in the Qur'an, such as His saying in "al-Dukhan": ﴿Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers] as a mercy from your Lord﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Dukhan: 5–6].

And His saying at the end of "al-Qasas": ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Qasas: 86].

And His saying at the end of "al-Anbiya'": ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107].

We have previously presented the verses indicating the use of "mercy" and "knowledge" for prophethood in surah "al-Kahf", in discussing His saying: ﴿And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Kahf: 65].

We have also previously presented the meanings of the use of "mercy" in the Qur'an in surah "Fatir", in discussing His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to people of mercy, none can withhold it﴾ up to the end of the verse [Fatir: 2].

As for His saying in this verse: ﴿We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in rank﴾, it means that He, the Exalted, did not delegate to them the affair of their livelihoods and their shares in this world. Rather, He—Majestic and Exalted—Himself undertook the distribution of that among them. So He made this one rich and that one poor, this one high and that one low, this one a servant and that one a master, and similar things. If He did not delegate to them their shares in this world, and did not make them judges over it, but rather He, the Exalted, was the one who disposes of it as He wills and how He wills, then how would He delegate to them the affair of sending down revelation, so that they could make decisions about whom the revelation descends upon?

This is something that is not rationally conceivable, and no one holds it except a foolish ignorant person like the disbelievers mentioned.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿that some of them may take others in service﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32]. The verified view, God willing, is that it is from "taskhir" (subjugation/employment).

The meaning of some of them subjugating others is that some of them serve others and work for others, because the order of the world in this life depends on its continuation upon that. Among His wisdom—Majestic and Exalted—is that He makes this one poor while being strong and capable of work, and makes that one weak who cannot work by himself. Yet Allah, the Exalted, provides for him dirhams with which he hires that strong poor man, so the strong one benefits from the weak one's dirhams, and the weak one benefits from the strong one's work; thus the livelihood is ordered for each of them, and so on.

These matters which Allah—Majestic and Exalted—mentioned in this noble surah have all come clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah.

As for their claim that Muhammad ﷺ is too lowly in honor and rank to have revelation sent down upon him, Allah mentioned it of them in "Sad" in His saying: ﴿Was the message sent down to him from among us? Rather, they are in doubt about My reminder﴾ up to the end of the verse [Sad: 8].

So the saying of the Makkan disbelievers: ﴿Was the message sent down to him from among us?﴾ means their denial that Allah would single him out for the descent of revelation from among them, on the claim that among them there is someone more deserving of revelation than him, because of the abundance of his wealth, his standing, and his nobility among them.

(p-113) The people of Salih said the same thing to Salih, as Allah said of them: ﴿Was the reminder cast upon him from among us? Rather, he is a liar, an insolent one﴾ [al-Qamar: 25].

So the hearts of the disbelievers are similar, and therefore their deeds are similar.

As Allah said: ﴿Thus said those before them, the like of their statement. Their hearts are alike﴾ [al-Baqarah: 118]. And He said: ﴿Did they bequeath this to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 53].

As for their proposal that revelation be sent down upon someone other than him from among them, and that they would not accept his being singled out for this to the exclusion of them—Allah mentioned this in surah "al-An'am" in His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah"﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. And His saying in "al-Muddaththir": ﴿Rather, every man among them wants to be given scrolls spread out﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52]—that is, that scrolls of revelation from heaven be sent down upon him, as Mujahid and others said, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

There is another well-known view regarding the verse.

As for His denial—Exalted is He—of the proposal that revelation be sent down upon other than Muhammad ﷺ, which is indicated by the interrogative hamzah that carries denial in His saying: ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾, to express their ignorance and their foolish minds—Allah has indicated it along with a severe threat in "al-An'am". For when He said: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will never believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah"﴾ [al-An'am: 124], He followed it, in response to them and in denial of their statement, with His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

Then He threatened them for that with His saying: ﴿Humiliation from Allah and a severe punishment will befall those who committed crime, for what they used to plot﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

As for Allah's being the one who undertook the distribution of their livelihood among them, it has come in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess so that they would be equal therein﴾ [al-Nahl: 71].

• And His saying: ﴿Look how We have favored some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction﴾ [al-Isra': 21].

• And His saying: ﴿Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾ [al-Zumar: 52].

• And His saying: ﴿And He sends down in measure whatever He wills. Indeed, He is Acquainted and Seeing of His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 27].

• And His saying: ﴿If he should be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both﴾ [al-Nisa': 135].

Allah has clarified the wisdom of this differentiation and variation in provisions, shares, strength and weakness, and similar things, by His saying here: ﴿that some of them may take others in service﴾, as has preceded.

As for His saying here: ﴿But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate﴾, it means that prophethood, guidance by the guidance of the prophets, and what the guided will attain on the Day of Resurrection are better than what people accumulate in this world of its trash.

Allah has indicated this meaning in other places, such as His saying in surah "Yunus": ﴿Say, "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate"﴾ [Yunus: 58]. And His saying in "Al 'Imran": ﴿And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate﴾ [Al 'Imran: 157].

Question

These noble verses cited here, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood﴾ (the verse), and His saying: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾ [an-Nahl: 71], and similar verses, indicate that the disparity among people in provisions and fortunes is one of the established sunan (divine laws) of Allah, the heavenly and cosmic, decreed by destiny, which none of the people of the earth can at all change or alter in any way: ﴿So you will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 43].

Thereby it is established that what the atheists today use as a pretext, those who deny the existence of Allah and all the prophethoods and heavenly messages, to plunder people's wealth and strip them of their private ownership of their property, under the claim of equality among people in their livelihoods, is a false matter that is impossible in any circumstance.

Moreover, they do not really intend what they claim; rather, they intend to monopolize the property of all people so that they may enjoy it and dispose of it as they wish, under the cover of many kinds of lying, deception and delusion, as every intelligent person acquainted with their conduct and their circumstances within their societies in their countries will realise.

So the small ruling clique and whoever joins them are the ones who enjoy all the good things of the country, while the rest of the common people are deprived of every good, wronged in everything, even of what they have earned with their own hands, and are fed with a ration card as mules and donkeys are fed.

Allah, exalted and majestic, had already known in His eternal knowledge that there would come people who usurp the wealth of others under the claim that this one is poor and that one is rich. He, exalted and majestic, forbade following desire under that claim, and threatened those who do not desist from it, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If he is rich or poor, Allah is more appropriate to both. So do not follow desire, lest you deviate. And if you distort or turn away, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ [an-Nisa: 135].

His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ contains a severe warning for whoever does that.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways [of silver] upon which they could ascend,﴾ ﴿and for their houses doors and couches [of silver] upon which they could recline,﴾ ﴿and ornaments of gold. And all of that would be nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. But the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.﴾

His saying: (li-buyutihim) in both places. Warsh, Abu 'Amr and Hafs from 'Asim recited it with a dammah on the ba' (lubyutihim), according to the original form.

Qalun from Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Shu'bah from 'Asim recited ﴿li-buyutihim﴾ with a kasrah on the ba' (libuyutihim), for the assimilation of the kasrah to the yā'.

His saying: (suqufan): Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim recited suqufan with two dammahs, as a plural.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited saqfan, with a fathah on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, as a singular intended to denote the plural.

His saying: ﴿wa-zukhrufan wa-in kullu dhalika lamma mata'u al-hayah﴾: Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir in the transmission of Ibn Dhakwan, and one of the two transmissions from Hisham, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya﴾ with the mim of (lamma) lightened.

'Asim, Hamzah and Hisham from Ibn 'Amir, and in one of the two transmissions, recited ﴿lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya﴾ with the mim of (lamma) doubled.

(p-116) The meaning of the noble verse is that when Allah explained the insignificance of the world and the greatness of the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32], He followed that with an explanation of its extreme insignificance, and that He made it shared between believers and disbelievers, and made what there is in the Hereafter of bliss specific to the believers and not the disbelievers. He explained the wisdom of the believer sharing worldly bliss with the disbeliever in His saying: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would be one community﴾, meaning: had it not been that We dislike all of mankind being one community united upon disbelief, We would have given all the ornaments of the world to the disbelievers.

But because We know the intensity of the inclination of hearts toward the splendour of the worldly life and their love for it, if We gave all of that to the disbelievers, the desire for the world would drive all people to become disbelievers. So We made in each of the disbelievers and the believers a rich one and a poor one, and We shared them in the worldly life.

Then He, majestic and exalted, explained the exclusivity of the bliss of the Hereafter to the believers in His saying: ﴿And all of that would be nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. But the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾, meaning: it is exclusively theirs, not others'.

This meaning has been made clear in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-A'raf": ﴿Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believed in the worldly life, purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection."﴾ [al-A'raf: 32].

So His saying: ﴿They are for those who believed in the worldly life﴾ means: shared among them in the worldly life; ﴿purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection﴾ means: specific to them and not the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, since the disbelievers have absolutely no share in the good things of the Hereafter.

So His saying in this verse of "al-A'raf": ﴿They are for those who believed in the worldly life﴾ is explicit in the sharing of believers with disbelievers in the enjoyment of the worldly life.

That sharing mentioned is indicated by the particle of non-existence for existence, which is (lawla), in His saying here: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would be one community﴾.

The specificity of the good things of the Hereafter to the believers, stated in the verse of "al-A'raf" by His saying: ﴿purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-A'raf: 32], is what He clarified in this verse of "al-Zukhruf" by His saying: ﴿But the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 35].

(p-117) All believers enter, in general, under the word "the righteous", since every believer has guarded himself against associating partners with Allah.

What these verses indicate, that He, exalted is He, gives the disbelievers of the enjoyment of the worldly life, is indicated by many verses of the Book of Allah, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "As for one who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126].

• And His saying: ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a harsh punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, your insolence is only against yourselves—[it is but] the enjoyment of the worldly life; then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Yunus: 23].

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed." [It is but] an enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 69–70].

The verses similar to these are many.

Allah has also explained in verses of His Book that His bestowing favours upon the disbelievers is not due to their honour with Him, but it is for istidraj (gradual enticement):

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So leave Me and whoever denies this statement; We will progressively lead them from where they do not know﴾ ﴿And I will give them time; indeed, My plan is firm﴾ [al-Qalam: 44–45].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the past of the wrongdoing people was cut off. And praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 44–45].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We replaced the bad state with good until they [forgot and] said, "Our fathers were touched by hardship and ease," so We seized them suddenly while they perceived not﴾ [al-A'raf: 95].

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Whoever is in error—let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension"﴾ [Maryam: 75], according to the more apparent of the two explanations.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin; and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178].

• And His saying: ﴿So I gave respite to the disbelievers; then I seized them, and how was My disapproval!﴾ [al-Hajj: 44].

The claim of the disbelievers that Allah gave them wealth and worldly bliss only because of their honour with Him and their deservingness of that, and that if the resurrection is true He will give them better than it in the Hereafter, Allah has refuted in many verses:

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is [because] We hasten to them with good? No, but they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55–56].

• And His saying: ﴿And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you nearer to Us in position, except for one who believes and does righteousness﴾ [Saba': 37].

• And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Your gathering has not availed you, nor [has] that which you used to be arrogant [about]"﴾ [al-A'raf: 48].

• And His saying: ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ [al-Masad: 2].

• And His saying: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into the Pit]﴾ [al-Layl: 11].

• And His saying: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We bestowed upon you﴾ [al-An'am: 94].

And other verses besides these.

We have already presented a portion of this in surah "al-Kahf", in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36].

Let us return to the explanation of the words of the noble verse. His saying: ja'alna means sayyarna (We made/rendered). His saying: ﴿li-buyutihim﴾ is a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) with repetition of the governing element from His saying: li-man yakfuru. On the reading suqufan with two dammahs, it is the plural of saqf, and the saqf of a house is well known.

On the reading saqfan with a fathah on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, it is a singular intended to denote the plural.

We have already presented at the beginning of surah "al-Hajj", in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Then We bring you forth as a child﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], that a singular noun which is a noun of genus (ism jins) may be used with the intention of the plural, and we gave many examples of that in the Qur'an and from Arabic evidences.

His saying: ﴿wa-ma'arija﴾: apparently it is the plural of mi'raj, without an alif after the ra'.

Al-mi'raj and al-mi'raj (sic: al-mi'raj and al-mi'raj) have the same meaning, and it is the instrument by which one ascends, i.e., goes up to the height.

His saying: (yazharun), i.e., they ascend and rise until they come to be on top of the houses. From this meaning is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they make a hole through it﴾ [al-Kahf: 97].

As-sururu is the plural of sarir, and al-ittika' is well known.

Al-abwab is the plural of bab, which is well known, and az-zukhruf is gold.

Az-Zamakhshari said: the ma'arij, which are the ascents, and the doors and the couches — all of that is of silver, as if he sees the conjoined and the conjoined-to as sharing in that. On this meaning, His saying: zukhrufan is an object whose governing element is omitted, and the estimation is: and We made for them, along with that, zukhrufan.

(p-119) Some scholars said: all of that is partly of silver and partly of zukhruf, i.e., gold.

Al-Qurtubi mentioned that the i'rab of His saying: wa-zukhrufan, according to this view, is that it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the meaning is "of silver and of zukhruf," so the preposition was deleted and zukhrufan became accusative.

Most grammarians hold that accusative by removal of the preposition is not regular or analogical, and what has been heard of it is preserved and not made a basis for analogy.

On this Ibn Malik proceeded in al-Khulasah, in his saying:

"And if it is deleted, the accusative for the governed is by transmission... etc."

And 'Ali ibn Sulayman, who is al-Akhfash al-Saghir, holds that it is regular in everything in which confusion is secure, as he indicated in al-Kafiyah in his saying:

"And Ibn Sulayman saw its regularity, if no confusion is feared, like 'from Zayd, he is far.'"

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And all of that would be nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 35] according to the reading of the majority, with the mim of (lamma) lightened, so (in) is the lightened form of the heavy one, and the lam is the distinguishing particle between the lightened (in) from the heavy and the negating (in), indicated by His saying in al-Khulasah:

"And in was lightened, so action became little, and the lam is obligatory when it is neglected."

And (ma) is extra for emphasis. As for the reading of 'Asim, Hamzah and Ibn 'Amir in one transmission from Hisham, (lamma) with the mim doubled, then (in) is negating, and (lamma) is a particle of affirmation in the sense of (illa).

The meaning: "And all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life."

Some of them mentioned that doubling the mim of (lamma) in some readings of this verse and in the verse of "al-Tariq": ﴿There is no soul but that over it is a guardian﴾ [al-Tariq: 4] is the dialect of the Banu Hudhayl ibn Mudrikah. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his constant companion.﴾ ﴿And indeed, they (the devils) hinder them from the way, while they think that they are guided.﴾ ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾

(p-120) We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Fussilat", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We appointed for them companions, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾ [Fussilat: 25].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you will be sharing in the punishment.﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this in "as-Saffat" (al-Saffat), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment.﴾ [al-Saffat: 33].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾.

We have already presented, at length, the verses that clarify this in surah "an-Naml" (The Ant), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾ [An-Naml: 80].

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to hold fast to the guidance of this great Qur'an, and He made clear to him that he is upon a straight path, meaning a clear way with no crookedness in it. This is the religion of Islam, which this great Qur'an contains, and which was revealed to him.

What this noble verse contains has also been made clear in other verses of the Book of Allah.

As for His command to him to hold fast to the great Qur'an, we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surah "al-Kahf" in our discussion of His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord; none can alter His words﴾ [al-Kahf: 27].

As for His informing him (ﷺ) that he is upon a straight path, among the verses that make this clear is His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We placed you on a [clear] way of the affair, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 18]. And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 52-53]. And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, you invite them to a straight path, but indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 73-74]. And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿So let them not dispute with you over the matter, but invite to your Lord; indeed, you are upon sound guidance, straight﴾ [al-Hajj: 67]. And His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾ [al-Naml: 79]. And other verses besides these.

(p-121) This verse of "al-Zukhruf" indicates that holding fast to this Qur'an is upon guidance from Allah, and this is known by necessity.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 45:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾.

What this noble verse includes, namely that all the messengers came with sincere monotheism (tawhid) to Allah, which is contained in the statement "There is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah), has been made clear in many verses, such as His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut (false deities)"﴾ [An-Nahl: 36].

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 25]. And that tawhid is the first thing that every prophet commands his nation to do.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [Hud: 50]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [Hud: 61]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [Hud: 61]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to Midian, their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah"﴾ — the verse [Al-A'raf: 85]. And other verses besides these.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly sent Musa (Moses) with Our signs to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs﴾ — the verse.

We have already presented the discussion of the story of Musa and Fir'awn in Surat al-A'raf and Surat Ta-Ha.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 48:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We seized them with punishment so that they might return.﴾

He does not specify here the type of punishment with which He seized them, but He clarified it in "al-A'raf" in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not be believers in you."﴾ ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood as distinct signs.﴾ [al-A'raf: 132–133]. And in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and a decrease in fruits﴾ – the verse [al-A'raf: 130].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "O magician, invoke for us your Lord by what He has covenanted with you. Indeed, we are [truly] guided."﴾ ﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word.﴾

What He, exalted and most high, mentioned in this noble verse, He clarified in "al-A'raf" with His saying: ﴿And when the plague fell upon them, they said, "O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove from us the plague, we will surely believe you and send with you the Children of Israel."﴾ ﴿But when We removed from them the plague at a term which they were to reach, at once they broke their word.﴾

The "ar-rijz" (plague) mentioned in "al-A'raf" is exactly the same as the "adhab" (punishment) mentioned in this verse of "az-Zukhruf."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and he can hardly express himself clearly﴾.

The discussion of this has already been presented in Ta-Ha, in the discussion of His saying about Musa: ﴿And loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, the verse [Ta-Ha: 27].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why have not bracelets of gold been bestowed upon him, or angels come with him in procession?﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of this in surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he would be a warner along with him?﴾ [al-Furqan: 7], and the verse that follows it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them﴾.

(Angered Us) means: they provoked Our anger and displeasure. That the intended meaning of "asaf" (anger/grief) is anger is indicated by its application to intense anger in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾ [Al-A'raf: 150], according to the more correct of the two interpretations.

Allah's statement: ﴿So We made them a precedent (salaf) and an example for the later ones﴾.

We have already discussed this in this noble surah, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed on﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in clamor], and they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not cite him to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾

Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and al-Kisa'i read this word (yaṣuddūn) with a ḍammah on the ṣād.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim and Hamzah read it (yaṣiddūn) with a kasrah on the ṣād.

On the reading with the kasrah, the meaning of (yaṣiddūn) is they clamor and cry out. It was also said: they laugh. And it was said: the meaning of the two readings is one, like (ya'rushūn) and (ya'rishūn), and (ya'kufūn) and (ya'kifūn).

On the reading with the ḍammah, it is from ṣudūd (turning away). The subject omitted in His saying (ḍuriba, "was cited") — the majority of the exegetes said it is 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari al-Sahmi, before his Islam.

That is: when Ibn al-Za'bari, the one mentioned, cited 'Isa ibn Maryam as an example, your people suddenly met it with clamor, shouting and laughter, out of joy at it and their assumption that Ibn al-Za'bari was your opponent. Or: their turning away from belief because of that example surprised you.

The apparent sense is that the particle (min) here is causal (sababiyyah, "because of"). It is well known that the grammarians of Arabic mention that among the meanings of (min) is causality, and among its instances is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a Fire﴾ [Nuh: 25]. That is: because of their sins they were drowned.

Among this is the saying of those swearing in the oaths of qasamah (collective oaths in cases of homicide): "I swear by God that he died because of his striking him."

The explanation of the meaning of Ibn al-Za'bari citing 'Isa as an example is this: when God revealed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you are to it bound to enter﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], Ibn al-Za'bari said: Muhammad (ﷺ) says that every object of worship besides God is in the Fire, and we and our idols are all in the Fire. And this 'Isa ibn Maryam, the Christians worshipped him besides God. So if the son of Mary is with the Christians who worshipped him in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be with him.

They said the same about 'Uzayr and the angels, because 'Uzayr was worshipped by the Jews, and the angels were worshipped by some of the Arabs.

It thus becomes clear that his citing 'Isa as an example — meaning, according to what he claimed Muhammad (ﷺ) said, that every object of worship and its worshipper are in the Fire — requires that 'Isa be an example for their idols in that all are in the Fire, although the Prophet (ﷺ) praises 'Isa with the finest praise, and makes clear to people that he is the servant of God and His messenger, and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him.

So Ibn al-Za'bari claimed that when the Prophet's (ﷺ) words required the equality of the idols with 'Isa in entering the Fire, while he (ﷺ) acknowledges that 'Isa is the messenger of God and that he is not in the Fire, this showed the falsity of his statement in his view.

At that point God revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us — they will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide eternally in that which their souls desire. The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ [al-Anbiya: 101–103], up to the end of the verse. And God also revealed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example﴾, to the end of the verse.

On this view, the meaning of His saying, ﴿They did not cite him to you except for argument﴾ is: they did not cite 'Isa as an example except for the sake of argument and contention in falsehood.

It was also said that (jadalan) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥal), and the use of an indefinite verbal noun as a circumstantial is common; we have explained its justification many times.

By argument (jadal) here is meant contention in falsehood, for the sake of victory without right.

A group of scholars said: the evidence that they intended argument with something they knew in themselves to be false is that the verse they used as a pretext for argument does not at all indicate what they claimed, and they are people of the tongue, the meanings of words are not hidden from them.

In the mentioned verse, God expressed with the word "ma" (what), which in its Arabic usage is for non-rational beings, because He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98], and did not say "man" (who). This is clear that the intended referents are the idols, and that it does not include 'Isa, 'Uzayr or the angels, as God clarified that He did not intend that by His saying after it: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Anbiya: 101].

Since they know from their language that the noble verse did not include 'Isa according to the requirement of their Arabic tongue, in which the Qur'an was revealed, we are certain that they cited 'Isa as an example only for the sake of argument and contention in falsehood.

As for the form of the plural in His saying, ﴿They did not cite him to you except for argument﴾, although the one who cited the example is one person, Ibn al-Za'bari, its justification goes back to two matters. The first: among the methods of the Arabic language is attributing the act of one man of a tribe to the whole tribe. Among the clearest Arabic evidences for this is the poet's saying:

؎ The sword of the Banu 'Abs, with which they struck, turned aside from the head of Khalid by the hand of Waraqa.

He attributed the striking to all of the Banu 'Abs, while stating explicitly that the sword was in the hand of one man of them, Waraqa ibn Zuhayr. The poet alludes by this to the killing of Khalid ibn Ja'far al-Kilabi of Zuhayr ibn Judaymah al-'Absi, and that Waraqa ibn Zuhayr struck the head of Khalid ibn Ja'far al-Kilabi, who had killed his father, with the sword of the Banu 'Abs, and it turned aside from him, that is, it had no effect on his head. The meaning of "nabā al-sayf" (the sword turned aside) is that it rose off the blow and did not cut.

The poet is satirizing the Banu 'Abs by this.

The wars that arose from this story, and the killing of al-Harith ibn Zalim al-Murri of the said Khalid, are all well known in their place.

The second matter: all the disbelievers of Quraysh approved of Ibn al-Za'bari's citing 'Isa as an example, rejoiced at it, agreed with him, and thus became like those who conspired together in it.

By these two mentioned matters the exegetes reconciled the plural form in His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ [al-A'raf: 77], and His saying: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Shams: 14], with the singular form in His saying: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took [the sword] and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Qamar: 29].

Some scholars said: the omitted subject in His saying: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example﴾ is the general body of Quraysh.

Those who said this argued that when the disbelievers of Quraysh heard the Prophet (ﷺ) mention 'Isa, and heard God's saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the example of 'Isa with God is like the example of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59], they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): You want by mentioning 'Isa only that we worship you as the Christians worshipped 'Isa.

On this view, the meaning is that they cited 'Isa as an example for the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the worship of people of each of them, claiming that he wants to be worshipped as 'Isa was worshipped.

On this view, the meaning of His saying: ﴿They did not cite this to you except for argument﴾ is: they cited this example only for the sake of contention in falsehood, although they know that you do not accept being worshipped in any way whatsoever.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we not worship except God and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of God"﴾ to the end of the verse [Al 'Imran: 64].

If this is from the Madinan Qur'an revealed after the Hijrah, its meaning is that the Prophet (ﷺ) repeated it to them many times before the Hijrah, as is known.

Likewise His saying: ﴿Nor would he order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to God]?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 80].

There is no doubt that the disbelievers of Quraysh were certain, throughout the entire period the Prophet (ﷺ) spent in Makkah before the Hijrah after the mission — thirteen years — that he called only to the worship of God alone, with no partner.

So their claim that he wants them to worship him is a fabrication on their part, while they know that they are fabricators in that.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Are our gods better, or is he?﴾

The verified view is that the pronoun in His saying "he" refers to 'Isa, not to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon both of them.

Some scholars said: their intention by the interrogation is to prefer their objects of worship over 'Isa.

It was said: because they take the angels as gods, and the angels are superior in their view to 'Isa.

On this view, their intention is that 'Isa was worshipped besides God and that did not cause him to be in the Fire, while our objects of worship are better than 'Isa, so how do you claim that they are in the Fire?

Some scholars said: they meant to prefer 'Isa over their gods.

The meaning on this view is that they say: 'Isa is better than our gods, that is, in your claim, while you claim that he is in the Fire by the requirement of the general sense of what you recite of His saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98].

And 'Isa was worshipped by the Christians besides God, so the implication of your statement that 'Isa is in the Fire, while you acknowledge otherwise, shows that what you say about us and our gods being in the Fire is also not true.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾, that is, obstinate, extreme in contention in falsehood, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And you warn thereby a quarrelsome people﴾ [Maryam: 97], that is, those intense in contention.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he is the most intense of adversaries﴾ [al-Baqarah: 204], because the form (fa'ila) with a fatha then kasra like (khasima) is one of the intensive patterns, as is known in its place.

You have known from what we have mentioned that His saying here: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example﴾, to the end of the verse, has been clarified by the verses we mentioned, by explaining its cause.

It is known that the meaning of a verse may become clear through explanation of its occasion of revelation.

On the first view, that they cited 'Isa as an example for their idols regarding entry into the Fire, that example is understood from the fact that the occasion of revelation of the verse is the revelation of His saying before it: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell﴾, since when it was revealed they said: if 'Isa is worshipped besides God like their gods, then they are equal in regard to what it indicates.

You have known the falsity of this from what we mentioned just above.

On the second view, that they cited 'Isa as an example for Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding 'Isa having been worshipped, and that he (ﷺ) wants to be worshipped as 'Isa was worshipped, then their cause for this is their hearing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the example of 'Isa with God is like the example of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59], and their hearing of the Meccan verses revealed concerning 'Isa, which clarify the meaning of the example.

As for the verses that explain His saying: ﴿They did not cite him to you except for argument﴾, their explanation of it is clear on both views. And God knows best.

The Words of Allah Most High: ﴿He is but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾.

The verified view is that the pronoun in His words "he" (هو) refers to Jesus as well, not to Muhammad, upon both of them be prayers and peace.

His words here, ﴿a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, do not specify here any of the favors which He bestowed upon His servant Jesus. However, He clarified that in "al-Ma'idah" in His words Most High: ﴿When Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [a figure] like the form of a bird by My permission, and you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission, and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission; and when you brought the dead out [alive] by My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 110]. And in "Al 'Imran" in His words Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near﴾ up to His words: ﴿and among the righteous﴾ [Al 'Imran: 45-46], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 61 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed it is a sign for the Hour, so do not doubt it﴾.

The verified position is that the pronoun in His saying "wa-innahu" refers to Jesus, not to the Qur'an, nor to the Prophet ﷺ.

The meaning of His saying ﴿a sign for the Hour﴾, according to the true and correct view which the great Qur'an and the mutawatir Sunnah testify to, is that the descent of Jesus at the end of time, alive, is a sign (ʿilm) for the Hour, that is, a sign of the nearness of its coming, because he is one of its portents (ashrat, the minor and major signs) which indicate its nearness.

The application of the term "sign of the Hour" to Jesus himself follows two matters, both of which are a well-known Arabic idiom.

The first of them: since the aforementioned descent of Jesus is a sign of its nearness, that sign became a cause of knowing its nearness. So in the verse the effect (musabbab) is mentioned and the cause (sabab) is intended.

The use of the effect while intending the cause is a well-known Arabic idiom in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs.

Among its examples in the Qur'an is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ [Ghafir: 13]. Provision (rizq) is an effect of rain, and rain is its cause; so the effect, which is provision, is mentioned while its cause, which is rain, is intended, because of the strong connection between cause and effect.

It is known that the rhetoricians and those who agree with them maintain that such a usage is of the type they call the metonymy (al-majaz al-mursal), and that the connection between cause and effect is among the relations of al-majaz al-mursal in their view.

The second of the two matters: the most that can be said is that the speech is by elision of a modifying noun (mudaf), the implied meaning being: "And indeed he is one possessing knowledge for the Hour," that is, "indeed he is the bearer of informing people of the nearness of its coming, by virtue of being a sign of it." The elision of the mudaf and the placing of the mudaf ilayhi in its position is common in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs, and the author indicated this in the Khulasa with his saying: "And what follows the mudaf will take its place in case of its i'rab when the mudaf is elided."

This latter is one of the two aspects by which the grammarians of Arabic explained the adjective being a verbal noun (masdar), as in your saying: "Zayd is generosity (karam), and ʿAmr is justice (ʿadl)," that is, "possessor of generosity and possessor of justice," as He said: ﴿And call to witness two just persons from among you﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]. He indicated this in the Khulasa with his saying: "They described with the masdar often, so they kept it in the singular and masculine."

As for the Qur'an's indication of this correct view, it is in His saying in Surah an-Nisa': ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [an-Nisa: 159], that is, he will surely believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus. This is explicit that Jesus is alive at the time of the revelation of this verse of an-Nisa', and that he will not die until the People of the Book believe in him.

It is known that they will not believe in him except after his descent to the earth.

If it is said: a group of the exegetes, from the Companions and those after them, went to the view that the pronoun in His saying "qabla mawtihi" (before his death) refers to the People of the Book, that is: "none of the People of the Book but that he will believe in him before the death of the People of the Book."

The answer is that the pronoun referring to Jesus is the view that must be adopted, rather than the other view, because it is preferable to it on four grounds. The first: it is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, the one that comes to mind from it, and the pronouns harmonize with one another under it.

The other view is contrary to this.

The clarification of this: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and their saying: "We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah"﴾, then He said: ﴿but they did not kill him﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿nor did they crucify him﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿but it was made to appear so to them﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿and indeed those who differ concerning him﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿are in doubt about it﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿they have no knowledge of it﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿and they did not kill him for certain﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿but Allah raised him﴾ (p-130) that is, Jesus; ﴿and there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him﴾ [an-Nisa: 159], that is, Jesus; ﴿before his death﴾, that is, Jesus; ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [an-Nisa: 157-159], that is, he, Jesus, will be a witness against them.

So this Qur'anic context which you see is apparent, with an apparentness that should not be departed from, that the pronoun in His saying "qabla mawtihi" refers to Jesus.

The second ground for preferring this view: on this correct view, the referent of the pronoun is stated explicitly in His saying: ﴿and their saying: "We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah"﴾ [an-Nisa: 157].

As for the other view, the referent of the pronoun is not mentioned in the verse at all; rather it is implied, its implied form being: "There is none of the People of the Book but that he will believe in him before his death," that is, the death of one of the People of the Book who is implied.

There is no doubt that what does not need an implied element is preferable and more fitting than what needs one.

The third ground for preferring this correct view is that the mutawatir Sunnah of the Prophet testifies to it, for the Prophet ﷺ has had hadiths narrated mutawatir from him that Jesus is alive now, and that he will descend at the end of time as a just judge (hakaman muqsitan). None deny the mutawatir status of the Sunnah on this except a stubborn person.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir, after mentioning this correct view and attributing it to a group of exegetes, the following text: "And this view is the truth, as we will clarify afterwards with the decisive proof, if Allah, the Exalted, wills." End of quote.

His saying "with the decisive proof" means the mutawatir Sunnah, because it is definitive (qat'iyyah), and he is right in that.

Ibn Kathir also said in his tafsir of this verse of az-Zukhruf the following text: "And the hadiths have been mutawatir from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a just judge." End of quote from him.

And he is right regarding the mutawatir status of the hadiths on this.

As for the claim that the pronoun in His saying "qabla mawtihi" refers to the Book (the People of the Book), it is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and no proof from the Book or the Sunnah supports it.

The fourth ground: the first, correct view is clear and free of difficulty, and needs neither interpretation nor specification, unlike the other view, which is problematic and hardly holds true except with specification. The interpretations that are narrated on this from Ibn ʿAbbas and others are plainly far-fetched and weak, because on the view that the pronoun in "qabla mawtihi" refers to Jesus, there is no difficulty and no obscurity, and no need for interpretation or specification.

As for the view that it refers to the People of the Book, it is very problematic with respect to every People of the Book who is overtaken by death, such as one who falls from a height to the ground, one whose head is cut off by a sword while unaware, one who dies in his sleep, and the like. This general statement in the verse does not hold true of this type of People of the Book unless one claims that they are excluded from it by a specifier.

There is no way to specify the generalities of the Qur'an except by a proof, which must be referred to, from the connected or disconnected specifiers.

As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he was asked about the People of the Book whose head is cut off, and he said: "Indeed his head speaks with belief in Jesus, and the one who falls from a height to the ground believes in him while falling" — its remoteness and weakness are not hidden, and there is absolutely no proof for it, as you see.

By all this you know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿before his death﴾ refers to Jesus, and that this verse of Surah an-Nisa' explains His saying here: ﴿And indeed it is a sign for the Hour﴾, as we have mentioned.

If it is said: many who have no verification claim that Jesus has died, and they believe what the misguided Jews and Christians believe, and they cite for that His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Me"﴾ [Al ʿImran: 55], and His saying: ﴿So when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117].

The answer is that there is absolutely no indication in either of the two verses that Jesus has actually died.

(p-132) As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿I will take you (mutawaffika)﴾, its alleged indication of that is negated on four grounds. The first: that His saying "mutawaffika" is a linguistic reality in the sense of taking a thing in full without deficiency; the Arabs say: "Fulan tawaffa his debt (dinahu), yatawwaha, so he is mutawaffin for it," when he received it and took it to himself in full without deficiency.

So the meaning of "Indeed I will take you (mutawaffika)" in the linguistic usage is: one who takes you to Me in full, with your soul and your body.

But the customary (ʿurfiyyah) reality has specified the aforementioned taking (tawaffi) to the seizing of the soul without the body. Regarding this kind of case, which lies between the linguistic and the customary reality, the scholars of usul have three schools of thought. The first: giving precedence to the customary reality and specifying the general scope of the linguistic reality by it.

This is the established position in the usul of ash-Shafiʿi and Ahmad, and it is the established position in the usul of Malik, except that in the furu' they sometimes did not adopt it in some issues.

To giving precedence to the customary reality over the linguistic reality, the author indicated in Maraqi as-Su'ud with his saying:
"The word is carried to the legal sense if there is none, then to the general customary sense;
so the linguistic is upon the clear, and there is no need to investigate metaphor in what has been chosen."

The second school: giving precedence to the linguistic reality over the customary, on the basis that the customary, even if it is preponderant through customary usage, the linguistic is preponderant through the original imposition.

This view is the school of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him.

The third school: neither the customary is given precedence over the linguistic, nor the linguistic over the customary; rather it is judged that both are equal and the two possibilities are balanced, so the word is judged to be ambiguous (mujmal), because of the possibility of this and the possibility of that.

This is the choice of Ibn as-Subki and those who agree with him. To these last two schools the author indicated in Maraqi as-Su'ud with his saying:
"The school of an-Nu'man is the reverse of what has passed, and the saying of ambiguity in it is approved."

(p-133) When you know this, know that on the first school, which is giving precedence to the linguistic reality over the customary, His saying ﴿I will take you﴾ indicates only that He took him to Himself with his soul and body, and does not indicate death at all, just as a creditor's taking his debt does not indicate the death of his debt.

As for the second school, which is giving precedence to the customary reality over the linguistic, the word "tawaffi" then indicates death in general.

But you will see, if Allah wills, that although it indicates that in general, it does not indicate that Jesus has actually died.

We have mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab," in Surah Al ʿImran, the reason it does not indicate the actual death of Jesus, namely His saying ﴿I will take you﴾. We said there, the text: "The answer to this is in three aspects. The first: His saying ﴿mutawaffika﴾ does not indicate a specific time, nor does it indicate that it has already passed; He will certainly take him at some day, but not that that day has already passed."

As for His conjoining ﴿and raise you to Me﴾ to His saying "mutawaffika," there is no evidence in it, because the majority of the people of the Arabic language agree that the waw does not require sequence (tartib) or joint occurrence (jam'), but only general conjunction (mutlaq al-tashrik).

Al-Sirafi and al-Suhayli claimed the consensus of the grammarians on this, and most attributed it to the verifiers, and this is the truth, contrary to what Qutrub, al-Farra', Tha'lab, Abu 'Amr az-Zahid, Hisham and ash-Shafi'i said, that it indicates sequence because of its frequent use in that sense.

Al-Sirafi denied that this view is established from al-Farra' and said: "I did not find it in his book."

Wali ad-Din said: "Our companions denied the attribution of this view to ash-Shafi'i." It was related from him by the author of ad-Diya' al-Lami'.

And His saying ﷺ: "I begin with what Allah began with" — meaning as-Safa — contains no proof that it requires sequence.

(p-134) The clarification of this is what al-Fihri said, as recorded from him by the author of ad-Diya' al-Lami'.

It is this: just as it does not require sequence or simultaneity, likewise it does not require their prohibition.

Furthermore, the particle *waw* may be used to link with the intention of giving priority to the first item, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158], according to the evidence of the hadith mentioned earlier.

It may also be that the conjoined item is meant to be in sequence, as in the verse of Hassan: "You satirized Muhammad, and I answered on his behalf," according to the narration with *waw*.

It may also be intended to mean accompaniment, as in His saying: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15], and His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon are joined together﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 9]. But *waw* is not to be read as indicating sequence or accompaniment except with a separate (explicit) evidence.

The second aspect: the meaning of *mutawaffika* is *munimuka*, "causing you to sleep." (And *rafi'uka ilayya*, "raising you to Me") means during that sleep.

The Qur'an has used the term *wafah* (taking/death) for sleep in His saying: ﴿It is He who takes you (*yatawaffakum*) at night and knows what you have committed by day﴾ [al-An'am: 60], and His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. Ibn Kathir attributed this view to the majority, and cited these two verses as evidence.

The third aspect: *mutawaffika* is an active participle from *tawaffahu*, meaning he took him and gathered him to himself. From this is the saying: "So-and-so *tawaffa* his debt," meaning he received it in full. So the meaning of *mutawaffika* according to this view is: "one who takes you from them to Me alive." This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari).

As for the reconciliation that Jesus was made to *tawaffa* (be taken) for hours or days and then was revived, there is no reliance on it, since there is no evidence for it. (End of quotation) from *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book).

We have already set forth in this discussion that the indication of His saying *mutawaffika* as a completed act of Jesus' death is negated on four grounds, and we have mentioned three of them without arrangement: (p-135) The first: *mutawaffika* is literal in its linguistic sense, meaning taking him with his spirit and body.

The second: *mutawaffika* is a descriptive term that may refer to the present, the future, or the past, and there is no evidence in the verse that this taking has occurred and passed. Rather, the widely transmitted Sunnah and the Qur'an both indicate otherwise, as we have clarified in this study.

The third: it was a taking by sleep, and we have mentioned the verses indicating that sleep is referred to as *wafah*. Thus both sleep and death are properly called *tawaffi*, and they are shared in customary usage.

These three aspects we have all mentioned in the passage we quoted from our book *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*.

We mentioned the first of them separately, in order to explain the positions of the scholars of *usul* (principles of jurisprudence) regarding it.

As for His saying: ﴿So when You took me up (*tawaffaytani*)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117], its indication that Jesus died is negated on two grounds. The first: Jesus says this on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no doubt that he will die before the Day of Resurrection. So his report on the Day of Resurrection of his death does not indicate that he has now died, as is clear.

The second: the apparent meaning of the verse is that he was taken (*tawaffi*) by raising and seizing the spirit and body, not a taking by death.

The clarification of this is that the contrast to that *tawaffi* is his remaining among them, in His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You took me up (*tawaffaytani*)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. This indicates that, for if it were a taking by death, He would have said "as long as I was alive, and when You took me up," since what is opposed to death is life, as in His saying: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾ [Maryam: 31].

As for the *tawaffi* that is contrasted with his remaining among them, the apparent meaning is that it is a taking by transfer from them to another place.

The most that can be said about this is that the word is taken in its literal linguistic sense with a clear indication against intending the customary sense, and there is no difficulty in this.

As for the fourth aspect mentioned earlier: those who claimed that Jesus had died said that there was no cause for that death except that the Jews killed him and crucified him. So when the negation of this cause is established, and they are certain that he did not die by any other cause, we are assured that he did not die at all. And that supposed cause is definitively negated without doubt, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾ [al-Nisa': 157]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they did not kill him with certainty. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 157-158].

The pronoun of His "raising" (*rafa'ahu*) is clearly referring to the raising of both body and spirit together, as is clear.

Allah, exalted is He, has explained the basis of the Jews' belief that they killed him: that Allah cast his likeness upon another man, so that whoever saw him firmly believed that he was Jesus.

So when they gathered together to kill Jesus, they saw him, and because of that likeness cast upon him they firmly believed he was Jesus, so they killed him.

Thus they believe in the truth of their claim that they killed him and crucified him. But the All-Knowing, the Subtle, the All-Aware revealed to His Prophet, in the Book which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, that they did not kill him and did not crucify him.

So Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who followed him have knowledge from Allah concerning the matter of Jesus, which the Jews and Christians did not have, as Allah made clear by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him with certainty. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 157-158].

The conclusion is that the Mighty Qur'an, according to the correct interpretation, and the widely transmitted Sunnah from the Prophet (ﷺ), both indicate that Jesus is alive, that he will descend at the end of time, that his descent is one of the signs of the Hour, and that the basis of those who claim they killed him, and those who follow them, is the casting of his likeness upon another, and their false belief that the man who was made to resemble Jesus was Jesus.

You have come to know the indication of revelation that this is false, and that His saying *mutawaffika* does not indicate his death as an actual event.

You have seen the explanation of this from four aspects, and that it is in accordance with what is established in the *usul* among the three schools of thought we mentioned. There is no difficulty in the fact that he did not die in actuality.

As for the view that gives priority to the literal linguistic meaning, the matter is clear, since on that view the verse does not indicate death.

(p-137) As for the view of the general (*ijmal*, ambiguity), what is established in the *usul* is that the ambiguous term is not to be applied to either of its two meanings, nor to all of its meanings, but the intended meaning must be sought through a separate evidence.

The Book here and the widely transmitted Sunnah have indicated that he did not die and that he is alive.

As for the view that gives priority to the customary meaning over the literal meaning, it is answered from several aspects. The first: the *tawaffi* is to be understood as sleep, and taking it that way falls within the category of the customary meaning.

The second: even if we grant that it is a taking by death, the form of the verb does not indicate that it has occurred as an actual event.

The third: the view mentioned about giving priority to the customary meaning applies only where there is no evidence diverting the meaning away from the customary sense to the literal sense. If such evidence exists, the literal meaning must be given priority, by unanimous agreement.

We have repeatedly stated that the indication of the Book and the widely transmitted Sunnah points here to the literal meaning and not the customary meaning.

Know that the view of giving priority to the literal meaning over the customary applies where the literal meaning has not been entirely abandoned. But if the literal meaning has been completely extinguished (*umitat*), it becomes obligatory to resort to the customary meaning by consensus (*ijma'*). And to this the author of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* (a versified work on the principles of jurisprudence) alluded in his verse:

"Is it consensus that if a literal meaning dies out, / its priority of application is established by the customary meaning?"

So if someone swears: "I will surely eat from this palm tree," the literal meaning requires that he does not fulfill his oath until he eats from the palm tree itself, not from its fruit.

But the customary meaning requires that he eats from its fruit, not from its trunk.

Resorting to the customary meaning here is obligatory by consensus, because the literal meaning in such a case has been completely abandoned, and no reasonable person would ever intend to eat from the trunk of a palm tree.

As for the literal meaning in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I will take you (*mutawaffika*)﴾, it is not among the abandoned literal meanings, as is clear.

It is known in the *usul* that the customary meaning is called a customary literal meaning (*haqiqa 'urfiyya*) and a linguistic metaphor (*majaz lughawi*), while the linguistic meaning is called among them a linguistic literal meaning (*haqiqa lughawiyya*) and a customary metaphor (*majaz 'urfi*).

(p-138) We have repeatedly stated that we have clarified that the Noble Qur'an contains no metaphor (*majaz*) in truth, in our treatise entitled *Man' Jawaz al-Majaz fi al-Munazzal li al-Ta'abbud wa al-I'jaz* (Prohibition of Metaphor in What Is Revealed for Worship and Miraculousness).

From all that we have mentioned, it becomes clear that this verse of *al-Zukhruf* is explained by the verse of *al-Nisa'* mentioned, that Jesus did not die, and that he will descend at the end of time. We said that His saying here: ﴿And indeed it is a sign (*'ilm*) for the Hour﴾ means a sign and an indication of the nearness of its coming, because the time of its actual arrival is known only to Allah.

We have repeatedly cited the verses indicating this.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it (*fa la tamtarunna biha*)﴾ means: do not doubt the establishment of the Hour, for there is no doubt about it.

We have repeatedly cited the verses clarifying this, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it﴾ [al-Hajj: 7].
• His saying: ﴿And warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt, when a party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shura: 7].
• His saying: ﴿He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ [al-An'am: 12].
• His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al 'Imran: 25].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾

We have already presented, many times over, the verses that make this clear, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir: 6], and His saying: ﴿Then do you take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf: 50], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 65:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So woe to those who have wronged, from the punishment of a painful day.﴾

His saying here, "zalamu" (wronged), means "kafaru" (disbelieved), as evidenced by His saying in Maryam, regarding the very same story: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a great day.﴾ [Maryam: 37]

His saying, "from the scene of a great day," is clarified by His saying here: "from the punishment of a painful day."

We have previously presented, many times, the verses indicating that the application of "zulm" (wrongdoing) to "kufr" (disbelief) is absolute, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, association [of partners with Allah] is a great wrong.﴾ [Luqman: 13]

• And His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254]

• And His saying: ﴿And do not invoke other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then you would be, at that time, among the wrongdoers.﴾ [Yunus: 106]

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have not mixed their faith with wrongdoing﴾ means with association (shirk), as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it in the authentic hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾

The interrogative particle hal (هَلْ) here carries the sense of negation, and yanzurun (يَنْظُرُونَ) means yantazirun (يَنْتَظِرُونَ), "they await." The meaning is: the disbelievers await nothing but the Hour, i.e., the Resurrection. ﴿That it should come upon them suddenly﴾ means in a state of it surprising them, i.e., coming upon them unexpectedly. ﴿While they do not perceive﴾ means they will not sense its arrival, being in a state of heedlessness and not feeling its approach.

The apparent view is that the verbal noun formed from anna and its clause in His saying ﴿that it should come upon them﴾ is in the accusative position, as a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion) for as-sa'ah (the Hour). That yanzurun is used in the sense of yantazirun is well known in the language of the Arabs, and among its examples is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"Indeed, if you two would grant me a single moment of time, it would benefit me before Umm Jundub."

What this noble verse contains, namely that the Hour will come upon them suddenly, is clarified in verses of the Book of Allah, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He, in "al-A'raf": ﴿It has been heavy in the heavens and the earth; it will not come upon you except suddenly﴾ [Al-A'raf: 187].

• His saying, exalted is He, in "Muhammad" (surah al-Qital): ﴿So do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come﴾ [Muhammad: 18].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They await not but one Blast, which will seize them while they are disputing. So they will not be able to make a bequest﴾ — the verse [Ya-Sin: 49–50].

So what is meant by the Blast is the Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest﴾, the verse, indicates that it will come upon them while they are in heedlessness and unaware of its coming, along with other verses. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve, those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned some of the attributes of those from whom fear and grief will be removed on the Day of Resurrection. He mentioned here faith in the signs of Allah and Islam, and He mentioned some of them in other places.

Among them is faith and God-consciousness (taqwa), as in His saying in the surah of Yunus: ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were conscious of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 62–63].

Among them is steadfastness (istiqamah) and saying "Our Lord is Allah." This is in His saying in Fussilat: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve"﴾ [41]. And His saying, exalted is He, in al-Ahqaf: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13]. And other verses besides these.

In the language of the Arabs, khawf (fear) is distress over a future matter.

And huzn (grief) is distress over a past matter.

Sometimes each of them is used in the place of the other.

And applying khawf to mean distress is a well-known Arabic style.

Some scholars said: From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿unless they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

He said its meaning is: unless they both know.

And from it is the saying of Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi:

"When I die, bury me beside a vine whose roots water my bones in the grave,
And do not bury me in the wasteland, for I fear, when I die, that I will not taste it."

So his saying "akhafu" means "a'lamu" (I know), because he has no doubt that he will not drink from it after his death.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims﴾ apparently indicates a difference between faith (iman) and Islam.

Some verses have indicated their identity, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We extracted from it those who were believers. But We found not there except one house of Muslims﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 35–36].

There is no contradiction in this, for faith (iman) is sometimes applied to everything to which Islam is applied, of belief and action, as is established in the Sahih in the hadith of the delegation of 'Abd al-Qays, and the hadiths of this kind are very numerous.

(p-141) Among the clearest of them in this regard is his saying (ﷺ): "Faith has more than seventy [branches]."

And in some of the authentic narrations in the Sahih: "And sixty-some branches, the highest of which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and the lowest of which is removing harm from the road."

So he (ﷺ) named "removing harm from the road" faith.

Al-Bayhaqi, may Allah have mercy on him, extended discussion in Shu'ab al-Iman, mentioning the deeds that the Book and the Sunnah have named faith.

Thus, complete legal faith (al-iman al-shar'i al-tamm) and complete legal Islam (al-islam al-shar'i al-tamm) have one meaning.

Faith may also be used in another sense, specifically for its greatest pillar, which is faith in the heart, as in the authentic hadith of Jibril.

The heart is a piece of flesh in the body: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and the rest follow it. On this basis, there is a difference in general between faith and Islam.

So faith, in this sense, is belief, while Islam encompasses action.

Know that His distinguishing between faith and Islam in His saying: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14].

Some scholars said: By faith here is meant its legal meaning, and by Islam is meant its linguistic meaning, because the submission of the limbs and their compliance without faith of the heart is Islam linguistically, not legally.

Other scholars said: By each of them is meant its legal meaning, but the negation of faith in His saying "and faith has not yet entered" is, according to those who say this, a negation of the perfection of faith, not a negation of its essence. But the apparent meaning of the verse does not support this, because His saying ﴿wa-lamma yadkhul﴾ (and has not yet entered) is a verb in a context of negation, and it is, verified, a form of generality, even if it is not emphasized by a verbal noun. Its basis is very clear, as we have mentioned repeatedly.

This is that the verb in its artificial (grammatical) sense is resolved into a verbal noun and a tense according to the grammarians, and into a verbal noun, a tense and a predication according to the rhetoricians, as they have verified in the discussion of metaphor (istiʿarah tabaʿiyyah), and this is more correct.

So the verbal noun is latent in the concept of the verb in its artificial sense by consensus, and it is an indefinite noun not made definite by anything, so it reverts to the meaning of an indefinite noun in a context of negation.

The author of Maraqi al-Su'ud has indicated that the verb in a context of negation or condition is among the forms of generality, in his saying:

"Like 'lā sharibta' or 'wa-in sharibā,' and they agreed that a verbal noun, if it has been brought, [it is general]."

And the reason for omitting (lā) in this verse, in His saying, exalted is He: "lā khawf" [al-Ahqaf: 13] — is that the second (lā), which is ﴿wa-lā hum yaḥzanūn﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13], is followed by a definite element, which is the pronoun, and it does not govern definites but indefinites. So when the omission of the second was required, the first was omitted too, so that the two particles would harmonize with each other in being omitted together.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Enter the Garden, you and your spouses, delighted.﴾
